Trash-hungry robots roam Japan’s busiest train station

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (594 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A jingle-playing, googly-eyed team of trash-collecting robots are vying to make the world’s busiest rail station a bit cleaner.
  • East Japan Railway Company (referred to as JR East), which runs several lines in Tokyo’s bustling Shinjuku Station, recently wrapped up a roughly 10-week trial of these eye-catching robots.
  • In a recent development, each of the three robots sports a different color (green, yellow, or red) to match their accompanying rail line.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A jingle-playing, googly-eyed team of trash-collecting robots are vying to make the world’s busiest rail station a bit cleaner.

East Japan Railway Company (referred to as JR East), which runs several lines in Tokyo’s bustling Shinjuku Station, recently wrapped up a roughly 10-week trial of these eye-catching robots. The machines stand just over three feet tall, and roll autonomously along preprogrammed routes through the station’s underground concourses between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m. Once full, they trundle back to the station’s garbage collection area on their own.

In a recent development, each of the three robots sports a different color (green, yellow, or red) to match their accompanying rail line. They definitely don’t look like your average sad, overflowing waste bin. Instead, they stroll up to commuters with bright lights and a front-facing screen showing cartoon eyes. Music appears to play when trash gets fed into them. An accompanying illustration of  Shinjukuma, the station’s bear mascot, demonstrates passengers which bins are for general trash and which are for plastic bottles. It’s all very Japanese.

JR East officials are hoping these bins on wheels will help relieve some of the burden on garbage collectors who struggle to keep up with trash generated by the millions  of people  passing through every day. The station, which sits on the western edge of central Tokyo, sees nearly three million daily passengers, an absurd amount of foot traffic that earned it a Guinness World Record. But more people means more trash. According to Tokyo Weekender, sanitation workers in the station unload garbage from fixed bags more than 10 times per day.

The robots could help, but only if they don’t get in the way and create more problems than they solve. Though JR East reportedly tested out a pair of garbage robots back in 2023, that was in a much smaller station and only for three days. Shinjuku is a much bigger challenge and serves as a kind of stress test to see if they are able to operate safely and effectively in densely packed areas.

Tokyo isn’t the only city experimenting with trash robots. A cat-themed, mobile trash unit made a brief appearance in Paris’ Charles De Gaulle airport last year. In Singapore, an autonomous robot started collecting garbage in 2019 at Jewel Changi Airport, the shopping complex attached to the city’s main airport. And while trash collection is still relatively niche, automated cleaning robots are swiftly becoming mainstays in many modern transportation hubs. Houston, Baltimore, Pittsburgh, and Oakland are among the many  cities in the United States already putting robot cleaners to work scrubbing and mopping airport floors.

It has been revealed that making these robots seem cute isn’t just for attracting selfies. It’s also a self-defense strategy. Humans have a mixed track record when it comes to sharing space with robots. In 2024, the New York Police Department retired a 400-pound, egg-shaped surveillance robot from patrolling subway lines after facing pushback from privacy activists and concerned citizens, some of whom felt uncomfortable near the lifeless, imposing monitor. Years earlier, a friendly hitchhiking robot called HitchBot made it about two weeks into its trip across the United States when it was found vandalized and beheaded in Philadelphia.

According to recent reports, could cartoon eyes and a cute mascot have saved those robots? It’s difficult to say, but at least the Tokyo garbage robots seemed to make it through their trial without any dissected parts. That’s an improvement.

Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale Is the Purest Prancing Horse in Years

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, nostalgia must be in the air in Maranello.
  • In the same vein as its predecessor, the 296 Challenge Stradale is a road car that shares its fundamental philosophy with the new 296 Challenge Evo racecar, which will debut in the single-marque Ferrari Challenge racing series next year.
  • See all results for Ferrari 296 for sale near 20147.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, nostalgia must be in the air in Maranello. A few months ago, Ferrari unveiled the 12Cilindri Manuale, reintroducing a (simulated) six-speed manual transmission to its model lineup purely for the sake of driver involvement. And now, the Challenge Stradale badge returns to the rear engine mesh of a Prancing Horse for the first time since the 360 CS was discontinued in 2004. Simply put, it's a good year to be a sentimental Ferrarista.

In the same vein as its predecessor, the 296 Challenge Stradale is a road car that shares its fundamental philosophy with the new 296 Challenge Evo racecar, which will debut in the single-marque Ferrari Challenge racing series next year. Parked side by side at their reveal at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya today, we would excuse a gentleman driver for confusing the CS with his new track-only machinery.

See all results for Ferrari 296 for sale near 20147.

There have been several limited-edition, track-focused mid-engine Ferraris since the 360 Challenge Stradale—including the F430 Scuderia, 458 Speciale, and 488 Pista—but the 296 Challenge Stradale goes the furthest of all of them in emulating its racecar counterpart, both aesthetically and mechanically.

While previous track-centric Ferraris have been somewhat demurely styled, the 296 CS puts its aerodynamic elements on full display. The carbon-fiber rear wing, dive planes, adjustable front splitter, and vented hood are essentially a copy-paste job from the Challenge Evo, with concessions made for road legality. Up front, twin vents positioned in the hood just before the windshield channel hot air expelled from two under-hood radiators over the windshield and towards the rear of the car, reducing the aerodynamic variations caused by changing ground clearance.

Recent findings suggest that other aero features are hidden out of sight. The CS's underbody has been smoothed to better feed the rear diffuser and work with three pairs of vortex generators at the front and two at the rear to generate additional downforce. With all of the aerodynamic elements colluding, the 296 Challenge Stradale makes 1360 pounds of downforce at 155 mph. That's a 72-percent increase over the base 296GTB's peak figure.

Recent findings suggest that big changes have been made to the CS's powertrain. You won't find any orange high-voltage wiring snaking around under the glass of its mid-mounted hood like you would in a 296GTB or 296 Speciale, as the 5-kWh battery pack and rear-mounted axial-flux electric motor have been removed entirely. The twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 operates unassisted and supposedly sounds better than ever courtesy of a reworked twin-exit exhaust system.

See all results for Ferrari 296 for sale near 20147.

In a recent development, overall firepower has decreased to 670 horsepower—149 ponies less than the standard 296GTB's. The upside is a notable decrease in mass, with Ferrari claiming that the removal of the plug-in-hybrid componentry played a major role in shedding 328 pounds from the 296GTB's dry weight. A lightened transmission flex plate, driveshaft, and timing cover were also developed to make the CS's powertrain as featherweight as possible. Without an electric motor present to fill in any thrust gaps left by turbo lag, the V-6 has been retuned to increase low-end grunt, although peak torque remains 546 pound-feet delivered at 6250 rpm.

As to be expected, yanking out an integrated powertrain system comes with some unique challenges that affect more than just the engine itself. For example, Ferrari was forced to enlarge the 296 CS's rear carbon-ceramic brake rotors and the ventilation ducts that cool them to compensate for the lack of regenerative braking. The decreased weight in the rear also shifted its weight distribution 1.5 percent to the front, which was addressed with suspension design and geometry changes.

The CS's newly developed suspension is derived directly from the 296 Challenge Evo and features semi-active dampers and a dual-spring design that improves rebound response. The result is reduced body roll, which helps the performance of the specially developed Pirelli P Zero R and P Zero Trofeo RS tires, measuring 245/35ZR-20 in the front and 305/35ZR-20 in the rear. The 20-inch forged wheels can be ordered in Matte Grigio Corsa, Matte Nero with a diamond-cut finish, or Matte Bianco Fuji.

The 296 Challenge Stradale's cockpit is very similar to the one found in the 296 Speciale. While niceties like climate control and a stereo remain, carbon-fiber door panels and a lack of armrests and storage pockets are a clear indication of the CS's weight-saving mission. For true gluttons for punishment, an even further stripped interior spec is available that removes the trim from the area beneath the seats and the lower section of the carpets beneath the center console, leaving part of the chassis exposed.

Ferrari is adamant that the 296 CS isn't a replacement for the 296 Speciale and will not cannibalize that model's customer base, as the two are intended for different buyers. Besides being geared less towards outright track duty, the 296 Speciale is a part of Ferrari's special series, meaning that customers need to have an "existing relationship" with the brand in order to get an allocation. The 296 Challenge Stradale is a standard range model, meaning anyone can walk into a dealer and order one, existing relationship or not. Ferrari says that it wants to court new Ferrari buyers interested in experiencing the purest driving experience that the prancing horse has to offer, and the 296 CS is the first step in that direction.

In a recent development, U.S. pricing has not been announced, but in its home market, the 296 Challenge Stradale costs 291,000 euros, or the equivalent of about $320,000. Stateside deliveries of the newly introduced CS are expected to begin sometime in late 2027. As a non-Speciale model, CS production numbers aren’t limited, which presents a unique opportunity to buy a special new Ferrari without already owning one.

Arc Raiders gets a few map exploit fixes in latest patch as Embark prepares to slow down how often patches are released

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders upgrade, and Embark has certainly delivered.
  • Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.
  • In a recent development, starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders upgrade, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

In a recent development, starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

In a recent development, on Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Industry observers note that alongside today’s patch, Embark also confirmed that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Recent findings suggest that now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more massive update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

Industry News: 3 Things to Do When Your Adult Child Pulls Away

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • Just last week, my parent coaching client looked at me quizzically while describing a recent text from her son.
  • It has been revealed that the client above was struggling with how to respond after a long lag in communication with her adult child.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

Just last week, my parent coaching client looked at me quizzically while describing a recent text from her son. The text was just a photo of her son's dog wearing (or at least trying to wear) a cap of a major league baseball team. She said, "Dr. Jeff, it's been two months since I last heard from him, and of course, I immediately smiled when I saw the pic. But I had no idea what to do next." This client elaborated that her fingers led her to compose and immediately delete five responses prior to sending them. She added, "No matter what I do, he will pull away again, anyway.".

It has been revealed that the client above was struggling with how to respond after a long lag in communication with her adult child. She didn't know whether to joke about the cute picture, or tell her son she missed him, or ask further about Thanksgiving. For any parents in similar situations, it can be maddening to feel unsure about how to respond.

Sources indicate that and, if you have not spoken to your adult child for over six months or even years, the absence of that relationship has a huge, seemingly constant presence. By this I mean that often in these partial or full-on estrangement situations, the reality is that minimal or no contact does not take away from the internal emotional upheaval that comes from the desire to reconnect.

It is easy to feel helpless in the face of not seeing your adult child or not having the level of connection that you value. In my parent coaching work, I encourage parents to focus on three things they can do no matter how long it's been since they last heard their grown child's voice.

Finish this sentence: "What I miss most about my grown child today is__________." Some parents might reply that they wish they knew how their son was doing. Maybe, as in the early example of the dog photo, a parent misses lighter moments of laughter. Maybe a song reminds you of your adult child.

Identifying what you miss is tangible and healthy because it helps you process difficult feelings like sadness, disappointment, nostalgia, or loneliness. For example, that treasured memory of you and your daughter going for a ride and belting out a shared favorite song may weigh heavily on your mind. Consider sharing these thoughts with trusted relatives, friends, a therapist, or a parent coach. Sometimes it helps to have someone just say, "Tell me more.".

According to recent reports, consider your adult daughter saying to you, "When I tell you what bothered me that you did when I was growing up, you kept twisting it to make it my fault and giving me advice." You may remember trying to help. But hold on, because, at the same time, maybe you can recall trying to give her advice when she said, "Dad, can I finish my point?".

Looking at your own behaviors in this way gives you an honest point of reflection to start. You could then say, "I've been reflecting on times I rushed in to give you advice, and it got in the way of better understanding what you were going through, and I'm sorry." This type of dialogue not only demonstrates that you are taking responsibility, but you are also modeling self-awareness to your adult child.

It has been revealed that in my book, You Ruined My Life—Now You Owe Me!, I explore how easily a parent's regret can turn into a feeling of indebtedness. In the parent coaching trenches, I have seen how tempting it is for parents to promise their adult children something to bring them closer. Please keep in mind that you can offer a sincere apology and still take your time to decide what you can reasonably do or give. For parents who are totally out of contact, I suggest you write down what you regret and keep it private.

This third point is really hard for parents missing their adult children. If several messages go unanswered, give your adult child room to reach out. If they asked for no contact, honor that request. Believe it or not, adult children in these situations often share with me that they still love and even miss their parents, even when they outwardly state they want no contact. Just remember what I wrote above: The absence of contact still has a great presence in both your mind and that of your adult child.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Subaru vehicles are known for their dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) capabilities, but to cut costs, the tech giant is now offering front-wheel-drive (FWD) versions on select electric models.

The Uncharted EV went on sale earlier this year as a smaller, sportier entry-level electric crossover positioned below the Solterra.

According to recent reports, it was also the first Subaru model in about 30 years not to come with standard all-wheel drive. After unveiling the Uncharted EV last summer, Subaru remarked, “For buyers focused on affordability and range, the entry-level Uncharted Premium FWD model will be offered in limited numbers.”.

According to recent reports, apparently, it wasn’t too limited. The 2027 Uncharted EV is now on sale, still with the base Premium FWD model equipped with a single 221-horsepower front-mounted electric motor.

Higher-priced Uncharted trims, including the Sport and GT, are upgraded with Subaru’s Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive system with X-Mode, delivering a combined 338 horsepower.

The 2027 Subaru Uncharted EV Premium FWD starts at $34,995, while the Sport and GT are priced from $39,795 and $43,795, respectively.

In the US, the 2027 Solterra and larger Trailseeker are still equipped with standard AWD, but Subaru is introducing new FWD (4×2) variants in some markets at a lower price point.

In comparison, the 2027 Subaru Solterra and Trailseeker EV start at $38,495 and $39,995, respectively.

Subaru opened preorders for its latest 2027 electric range in Spain, including the Unchartered, Solterra, and E-Outback, which is sold as the Trailseeker in the US.

According to recent reports, all of which will be available with a lower-priced FWD variant. Like the Uncharted, Subaru will still offer AWD on higher-priced Solterra and E-Outback trims.

The fresh Subaru Uncharted (4×2) starts at €26,525 ($28,900), the Solterra (4×2) starts at €35,025 ($38,200), and the E-Outback (4×2) starts at €36,525 ($39,800) in Spain, including subsidies, discounts, and other incentives.

Preorders are open for the Uncharted, while the Solterra and E-Outback are expected to launch in mid-2027.

Will Subaru expand FWD (4×2) to other vehicles and markets, like the US? The Uncharted is still Subaru’s only EV sold with standard FWD. The 2027 Solterra and Trailseeker are equipped with AWD and X-Mode.

Recent findings suggest that for a small electric car driven on pavement I prefer RWD, which offers less complexity, better uphill traction, and a tighter turning circle. I love the handling of my last two cars, a RWD Miata and a RWD BMW i3 (old style).

Subaru is already selling considerably more EVs in the US, with three affordable, practical electric SUVs: the Uncharted, Solterra, and Trailseeker.

According to recent reports, in Spring 2027, it will add its first three-row electric SUV, the Getaway. It wouldn’t be a surprise to see Subaru introduce a FWD option for other models, like the Solterra, at a lower price point.

Then again, AWD is used significantly more in the US than in Spain and other markets. For now, the Uncharted remains Subaru’s sole FWD model.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Only four months after setting its own record, the European Space Agency’s (ESA) Euclid space telescope has outdone itself yet again. In a study published today in the journal Astronomy and Astrophysics, ESA researchers announce the discovery of the most distant—and therefore oldest—quasar ever observed. The object now classified as J1504+6252 formed just 630 million years after the substantial bang, making it 40 million years older than the quasar Euclid spotted in July. Euclid’s latest image is equivalent to viewing J1504+6252 as it existed about 13.1 billion years ago, when the universe was only five percent its current age.

Sources indicate that A quasar is the result of a galactic core’s supermassive black hole inhaling cosmic gas and dust while simultaneously spewing tremendous amounts of energy. During this comparatively brief phase in a galaxy’s lifecycle, the nucleus can actually shine brighter than the entire system itself. But even such a luminous object like quasar J1504+6252 can be hard to spot when it is located deep within space-time.

However, Euclid excels at finding these and other elusive objects. The ESA rolled out its space telescope in 2023 to examine the mysterious realm of dark matter and dark energy. Despite estimates that these forces account for about 95 percent of the universe, astronomers still know very little about them. Identifying subjects like quasars allows researchers invaluable opportunities to learn more about dark matter and dark energy, as well as their roles in the early, formative eons of the cosmos.

In a recent development, J1504+6252 is so young and gargantuan that it’s confounding astronomers. Based on their initial assessments, it’s unclear how a quasar with a mass equivalent to about 360 million suns even formed so early in cosmic history.

Industry observers note that it also has the largest redshift on record. Redshifting occurs when light waves stretch towards the infrared spectrum as they travel through the universe. The greater the redshift, the older its source is. In barely 1.5 years, Euclid has flagged 31 quasars, including 12 beyond a redshift of 7.

J1504+6252 is the first quasar to possess a redshift beyond 8. Despite its age, J1504+6252 is devouring material at a comparatively slow pace. This implies it attained its size during unprecedentedly fast growth spurts early in its life—a feature that challenges existing models of black hole formation.

Sources indicate that astronomers have nicknamed the quasar Dún Aonghasa to honor its age and location. The actual Dún Aonghasa is a prehistoric clifftop fort in Ireland overlooking the Atlantic Ocean. Like the ancient structure itself, J1504+6252 is situated at the edge of the visible cosmos. That remarked, astronomers expect Euclid to find multiple more quasars beyond redshift 8 in the years to come.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the United Kingdom-based researchers found that only 12% of UK plant-based milk, yogurt, and cheese products analyzed were fortified with iodine.
  • In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) provides guidance on the nutritional content of PBAs, but fortification with iodine is voluntary.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Replacing dairy with plant-based alternatives (PBAs), even partially, could substantially lower iodine intake, especially if those alternatives aren’t fortified, according to a recent study published in the Lancet Planetary Health.

In a recent development, the United Kingdom-based researchers found that only 12% of UK plant-based milk, yogurt, and cheese products analyzed were fortified with iodine. This compares with 61% for calcium and 46% for vitamin B12.

In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) provides guidance on the nutritional content of PBAs, but fortification with iodine is voluntary.

The study found that replacing as little as 20% of dairy intake with plant-based alternatives could increase the risk of inadequate iodine intake, particularly among adolescent girls and women of reproductive age.

“People often worry about a decline in calcium intake when they replace some of their dairy with plant-based alternatives. As a result, iodine is frequently overlooked. This study serves as a valuable reminder of iodine’s significance as a nutrient,” said Victoria Finn, MD, board certified endocrinologist at Medical Offices of Manhattan, who wasn’t involved in the study.

The study included analysis of UK plant-based milk, cheese, and yogurt products, as well as dietary data from 3,500 people.

The researchers used statistical modeling to predict how swapping dairy for PBAs might affect iodine and other nutrients.

The people who are most vulnerable to iodine inadequacy are adolescent females and people at reproductive age, especially those who are pregnant or who plan to become pregnant.

The researchers estimated that replacing 20% to 35% of dairy intake with PBAs would increase the proportion of people with inadequate iodine intake:.

According to recent reports, when the researchers modeled the replacement of all dairy products with PBAs, the proportion of adolescent females with inadequate iodine intake rose to 80%. Among females ages 19 to 49, that proportion remained relatively stable as replacement rates increased.

It is key to keep in mind that the study used dietary modeling rather than direct measurement of iodine status.

Iodine is notable for thyroid hormone production, metabolism, and both fetal and child brain development.

“Your thyroid gland requires iodine to produce thyroid hormones, which play a crucial role in regulating metabolism and supporting normal growth and development,” stated Finn.

It has been revealed that she added that if you consistently consume too little iodine over an extended period, the thyroid gland may enlarge and eventually struggle to produce enough hormones. This condition is known as hypothyroidism, which can lead to various symptoms such as lethargy, sleepiness, weight gain, dry skin, and more.

“Hypothyroidism can be particularly dangerous during pregnancy, as the baby’s brain, nervous system, and organs rely heavily on the mother’s thyroid hormone during the early stages of development,” Finn added.

In the United Kingdom, dairy is a major iodine source due to cattle feed supplementation, not because dairy is naturally high in iodine.

In the United States, dairy is also an key source of iodine for the same reasons.

In a recent development, however, the risk profile for iodine deficiency in the U.S. may differ from the U.K., as iodized salt is also a significant source of iodine and is widely available in the U.S., but not in the U.K.

According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the recommended daily intake of iodine depends on your age.

Recent findings suggest that plant-based or plant-forward diets have grown in popularity, in part due to the health benefits they offer. For example, consuming less meat can reduce your risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and high cholesterol.

However, as this study suggests, it may be possible to reduce your iodine intake when transitioning to a plant-based diet. There are ways you can protect your iodine intake when choosing a more plant-forward diet, though.

It has been revealed that check the labels on plant-based dairy alternatives to find those fortified with iodine. You can also read the nutrition label. Iodine may be listed as potassium iodide or potassium iodate.

Seafood, eggs, and iodized salt are all good sources of iodine.

You can also discuss iodine supplements with your healthcare professional.

Industry observers note that “Iodine supplements should be taken with caution, especially without checking your thyroid levels,” said Finn. “Additionally, be cautious with kelp supplements, as their iodine content can vary, and excessive iodine intake can disrupt thyroid function.”.

Either way, she suggests hitting the weights two to three times a week without going all-out every session.

Recent findings suggest that but if you’re running and strength training, consider also building your explosive power. “You have to train the spring, train that reactive quickness,” Conley notes. And, this comes in handy whether you’re sprinting, changing direction on the court, or charging uphill. It will also help your big lifts in the gym, particularly squats, deadlifts, and any type of Olympic lift because it develops things like neuromuscular coordination—allowing you to implement full-body movement patterns and stabilize heavy loads faster; and the rate of force development—how fast you can turn your strength on.

Just make sure you train this way early in your workout, not at the end. “You don’t want to do plyometric training when you’re fatigued,” Conley cautions. Doing so can compromise your form, making those explosive moves less effective and potentially increasing your risk of injury.

THE BODYPART THAT makes all of this training possible is your feet. Their small muscles help you maintain balance, support your arches, and control movement under load. During a squat, for example, those muscles help provide a stable base as you drive through your legs and hips. “Deadlifting is a foot action,” Conley explains. “You’ve got to feel your mid foot and press it into the ground to stabilize your body.”.

Running demands just as much. Every stride is essentially a single-leg hop, with your feet and ankles absorbing impact, storing energy, and releasing it to propel you forward. In her practice, Conley sometimes sees clients with weak feet or Achilles challenges. “When they go to hop, they sink into the ground, and there’s just no spring out of that system.” It’s one more reason those muscles below your ankles deserve just as much attention as your quads and glutes.

And while you could do specific mobility exercises for your feet, those small muscles get quite a workout when performing single-leg moves that help build strength, balance, and stability.

When a tom turkey is relaxed, the fleshy growth above his beak is short and stubby, like a little unicorn horn. But when he struts to attract mates or establish dominance, blood rushes into the growth, known as the “snood.” The snood then swells and lengthens until it drapes over the turkey’s beak like a long pink earring. Turkey hens have snoods too, but theirs are smaller. So why would a male bird grow something that looks so impractical?

In a recent development, dr. Richard Buchholz, a professor of biology at the University of Mississippi, is the best person to ask. Features of bird anatomy that seem more decorative than useful, which biologists call “ornaments,” have long fascinated Buchholz. For his master’s degree, Buchholz studied the yellow-knobbed curassow, a South American bird with a bright yellow knob on its bill and a crest of curly feathers.

It has been revealed that [ Related: How did Thanksgiving turkeys get so darn massive? ].

Industry observers note that when it came time to choose a PhD topic, his advisor suggested a more common bird: the wild turkey. Buchholz wasn’t keen. “I don’t wanna be the turkey guy,” he told his advisor. Still, he gave it a try. More than three decades later, he’s still studying them. And his research has shown that turkey snoods have at least two functions: seduction and status.

According to recent reports, it turns out that snoods are tools of seduction. In a 1995 study by Buchholz that used both live male turkeys and decoys, females showed a distinct preference for males with longer snoods and wider skullcaps. (The skullcap is the smooth patch of bare skin on top of a tom’s head.).

This was surprising because male turkeys have several ornaments, including a beard that grows from their breast area, iridescent feathers, and a tail fan similar to that of a peacock. Yet females seem to care more about the snood and skullcap.

Recent findings suggest that lady turkeys are discerning birds. In some trials, females were choosing between two males whose snoods differed by “just a couple millimeters,” Buchholz indicates—and they still went for the longer one.

Industry observers note that he found a likely reason for this preference in male turkeys’ guts. Males with longer snoods had fewer coccidia in their digestive tract. Coccidia are single-celled parasites that damage the lining of the intestine and can be fatal in young animals.

Recent findings suggest that buchholz thinks that snoods are indicators of health, allowing females to assess a male’s quality as a mate just by looking at them. A long snood signals a male whose immune system is strong enough to fight off parasites like coccidia, and who may pass on that disease resistance to their offspring, thus improving their chances of survival.

How do birds stay warm in winter?

Do animals really mate for life?

It has been revealed that why are some animals so colorful? Blame this pigment.

It has been revealed that why do hummingbirds buzz? Tiny tornadoes.

Real-life vampire birds hunt and drink blood in remote Ecuador.

From chirps to ‘hellos’: Why some birds talk like people.

Another set of experiments, which Buchholz published in 1997, suggests that male turkeys also use snoods to size up the competition.

Buchholz trained captive male turkeys, each housed on its own, to enter an arena where bird seed was waiting. “They love bird seed,” Buchholz says. “Normally, in captivity they’re fed dry pelleted food, so they love anything that looks like a natural grain or seed.”.

Industry observers note that when Buchholz let two males enter the arena at the same time, they rarely engaged in a physical fight over the treat. “Almost always, one male would give up,” Buchholz notes. “The male with a longer snood typically would not be the male who gave up.”.

Recent findings suggest that to check that the snood itself was what mattered, he ran the trials again with two plastic decoys that differed only in snood length. “And most of the males chose to eat the seed in front of the turkey decoy with the shorter snood of the two,” Buchholz notes.

According to recent reports, A turkey’s bare head and neck are covered with featherless nodules, called caruncles, which can shift in color from red or pink to white or blue. Toms have much larger caruncles than hens. “Their color can change really dramatically at different points in a male’s display,” Buchholz says.

But what it means is unknown. Buchholz suggests that the redness, rather than the size, could hint at anemia in the male, but admits that that’s just conjecture.

Recent findings suggest that buchholz hasn’t directly studied the function of turkey caruncles. But as part of a 2024 study he did with Rebecca Kimball of the University of Florida, he found that bare skin helps galliform birds—a group that includes turkeys, chickens, and pheasants—to lose heat and to attract mates. So caruncles may help keep a tom cool while he catches a hen’s eye.

Sources indicate that the balancing act between body temperature regulation and courtship is the focus of Buchholz’s current research. He and his team are investigating whether rising spring temperatures affect males’ ability to display to females, and whether males choose display times and places that help them manage heat.

According to recent reports, buchholz has also made peace with his reputation. “I came to embrace the title of Turkey Man,” he notes. “They’re really fascinating, socially interacting creatures.” As his research has shown, their anatomy is key to how they behave with each other. Those impractical-looking snoods are actually useful messaging tools—even if us humans might not find them as attractive as lady turkeys might.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A research letter, published in JAMA Pediatrics, analyzed data on approximately 11 million infants from 2017 to 2025 and found that vitamin K administration declined from 97.7% to 95%, while cases of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) nearly quadrupled.
  • It has been revealed that A second study published in JAMA, based on data from 5.2 million U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two large studies published on November 5 link declining newborn vitamin K shot rates to a sharp increase in infant bleeding cases, including potentially fatal brain hemorrhages.

A research letter, published in JAMA Pediatrics, analyzed data on approximately 11 million infants from 2017 to 2025 and found that vitamin K administration declined from 97.7% to 95%, while cases of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) nearly quadrupled.

It has been revealed that A second study published in JAMA, based on data from 5.2 million U.S. infants, found that refusal rates more than doubled, rising from 3.1% in 2017 to 6.8% in 2025. Infants who did not receive the shot had a 47% higher risk of bleeding and more than twice the risk of intracranial bleeding.

Additionally, latest data from Truveta suggest the trend is continuing: refusals of vitamin K shots increased by 57% between January and June 2026, rising from 5.2% to 8.1% of newborns.

Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting, and newborns naturally have very low levels. Without the preventive injection, infants are at risk for VKDB, which can cause sudden bleeding in the brain, gastrointestinal tract, and other organs. Late-onset VKDB can occur up to six months after birth, often without warning signs, and may be fatal.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) continue to recommend an intramuscular vitamin K injection for all newborns, ideally within 6 hours of birth.

The shot is not a vaccine; it is a nutrient injection that helps prevent dangerous bleeding. A single dose reduces the risk of late-onset VKDB by approximately 98%.

Experts not involved in the studies attribute the rise in refusals partly to broader vaccine hesitancy and mixed public health messaging.

“The decision to vaccinate a newborn or allow a vitamin K injection at birth is complex, with multiple factors playing a role in the ultimate decision,” remarked Graham Tse, MD, a pediatrician and chief medical officer of MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, CA.

Some of these factors, Tse remarked, include conflicting messages from federal health agencies such as the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), both overseen by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., an outspoken critic of the childhood immunization schedule.

The vitamin K shot is not a vaccine, yet RFK Jr. has declined to reassure parents about its safety, despite the CDC’s current recommendation to administer it at birth.

Additionally, growing medical distrust among parents has led to refusal of routine newborn care, such as the vitamin K shot, Reuters reports.

Healthline spoke with Tse to learn more about the risks of refusing the vitamin K shot and what new or expectant parents should know about this routine newborn treatment.

This interview has been lightly edited and condensed for clarity and length.

Tse: The decision to vaccinate a newborn or allow a vitamin K injection at birth is complex, with multiple factors playing a role in the ultimate decision.

A contributing factor to the decline in vitamin K injection at birth, as well as in newborn hepatitis B vaccination, is the conflicting messages from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Recommendations from these entities and others are conflicting or do not align with established, research-based, and proven recommendations from organizations such as the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and the Infectious Diseases Society of America.

When there are conflicting recommendations, it creates confusion and doubt among parents about what the best or right choice is for their child.

As well, there is so much misinformation on the internet, among influencers, and on social media that it is difficult to know what information is accurate, well-researched, and proven, versus what may be just someone’s opinion or belief.

Some are mistaking the vitamin K injection at birth for a vaccination, which it is not. Ultimately, all these factors are contributing to parents declining or delaying vitamin K injections at birth.

In a recent development, tse: Declining the newborn vitamin K injection puts the newborn at significant risk of serious and life threatening complications from vitamin K-deficient bleeding (VKDB). This was previously referred to as hemorrhagic disease of the newborn.

VKDB can be as mild as bruising of the skin but can be as serious as bleeding into the brain, and newborns and infants can die from VKDB.

Declining vitamin K injection at birth is significant because of the serious and potentially life threatening consequences of deficiency of Vitamin K and not being able to clot the blood.

The vitamin K injection at birth is highly effective at preventing VKDB.

Tse: If a neonate or infant has vitamin K deficiency, the ability to clot their blood and stop bleeding is highly reduced.

All newborns are at risk of low vitamin K due to low body stores, low vitamin K content of breast milk, reduced ability of the gut to mobilize vitamin K, and poor transfer of vitamin K across the placenta.

When the blood cannot clot, bleeding from minor or minimal trauma can occur, and even bleeding without injury or trauma may occur. This can include bruises, bleeding from the mouth or gastrointestinal tract, bleeding from cuts or circumcision.

Bleeding can occur anywhere in the body, including in the brain, which can be catastrophic.

VKDB can occur from birth and through several months of life. Bleeding in the brain from VKDB, one of the most serious consequences, can occur at any time from birth to up to 6 months or so and can occur unexpectedly and suddenly. Vitamin K given at birth can prevent this risk of bleeding.

Tse: Vitamin K is a necessary vitamin that all humans need. Vitamin K is not a vaccination.

Newborns need vitamin K to prevent serious, significant, and often catastrophic bleeding during their first several months of life.

Vitamin K has been given to newborns in the United States for close to 70 years, is safe, is studied, and is proven to help prevent vitamin K-deficient bleeding.

I urge newly introduced parents to allow their newborns to receive the vitamin K injection at birth — it protects them, keeps them healthy, is proven safe, and is recommended.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Red Dog Mine in Alaska burns about 40,000 gallons of diesel a day to keep one of the world’s largest zinc mines running, and now, an 8.8-megawatt (MW) solar farm and battery storage will help cut that fuel use.

The Alaska Energy Authority’s board unanimously approved a nearly $5 million loan for the project through its Power Project Fund. Tugliq Red Dog1 will build, own, and operate the roughly $35 million solar project and sell the electricity to mine operator Teck Alaska. The state’s loan review notes site work began in June and expects the solar and storage to come online in October 2028.

Red Dog sits about 105 miles north of the Arctic Circle, on land owned by NANA, an Iñupiat-owned Alaska Native corporation. The array would be larger than any solar farm operating in Alaska today, as KOTZ’s Desiree Hagen reported for Alaska Public Media. Hagen reported that the aims call for more than 15,000 panels across around 30 acres.

The mine gets all its power from on-site diesel generators. In summer, it can draw so much electricity that Teck has to cut power elsewhere at the site. The solar array and the 8.8 MW, 15 megawatt-hour (MWh) battery will give the operator another source of power during those crunches.

The state of Alaska expects the solar and storage project to cover about 5% of the zinc mine’s electricity needs under its current operating plan. The project could do even more after mining ends, covering about 90% of the site’s annual electricity needs.

Cost to import sun to a remote Alaskan village 0, cost to import diesel quite high.

A 500W panel weighs 60 lbs about the same as 9 gallons of diesel. 500W panel generates 750kwh of electricity a year each and every year for 20 years. 9 gallons of diesel gives you 350kwh of thermal energy which yields varying amounts of desired output.

Recent findings suggest that teck expects the mine’s existing deposits to support operations through 2031, and it’s studying whether to develop two nearby deposits. If that expansion goes ahead, the state projects the solar and battery project would cover about 3% of the larger operation’s electricity needs. If mining ends, demand will drop sharply, but the site will still need electricity for cleanup and long-term water treatment.

Industry News: The Courage to Question Our Own Certainty

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • There are a plethora of potentially polarizing concerns these days in all aspects of our lives!
  • Sources indicate that our positioning and decisions on an issue seem like they happen in the blink of an eye.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

There are a plethora of potentially polarizing concerns these days in all aspects of our lives! It seems that we can hardly get a point of view on the table before a fellow conversationalist debunks our idea and discredits us along the way. Take your pick from a bushel full of igniting issues, whether it be global warming, wars, increasing the tax percentage for the very wealthy, or the strengths and weaknesses of our favorite political personalities; there will be no shortage of strong opinions. You can also be assured that before the full set of points of view are exposed or explored, one or more folks will have already decided what the correct point of view should be.

Sources indicate that our positioning and decisions on an issue seem like they happen in the blink of an eye. This instant judgement can create ill will, stress for us and the other, and can challenge or ruin long-standing relationships. Furthermore, it will likely lead to a suboptimal exploration and resolution of the salient points of view. The pivot that I would like to explore is realizing that although our interpretations and positions usually feel quite certain to us, they most likely do not represent the whole of the reality of that situation; they are a narrower, biased slice of the problem or solution.

I would like to explore what can happen when we can loosen our grip on our story/point of view, and instead consider what might ensue if we instead question our own certainty. This, of course, would require slowing down enough to really listen first and then explore the fuller reality of the situation together; then, with skillful listening and openness to other ways of thinking, we can have a meaningful and civil dialogue.

Industry observers note that we seem to be experiencing a plethora of fractured conversations, competing accounts of the truth, information overload, and fear about the future, all of which are leading to what we might call “contemporary exhaustion.” And if the impact of this on us personally wasn’t enough, the relational tension as well as the societal and political challenges are at an all-time high. It is so much more likely that answers to our difficult questions will land somewhere in the middle of the two opposing extremes being debated, or in a yet-to-be-discovered “third alternative” idea that cannot possibly be uncovered because of the anger, tension, and lack of listening in the interchange. Just to ground this idea in one statistic: the American Psychological Association's Stress in America survey, "A Crisis of Connection," reported that 62% of adults considered societal divisions a significant stressor in their lives.

Sources indicate that if you are willing to have the “courage to suspend the certainty” of your initial interpretation and allow for more information, thoughts, and feelings to emerge between you and another, amazing things can happen. Try following a simple practice of what I will call “thoughtful receptivity” using these 4 steps. Imagine that, before you know it, you are in a polarizing conversation with challenging points of view and heated feelings emerging. Each side draws his/her sword, and the point-counterpoint debate begins. You have enough presence to realize you are in the battle, and it likely will not end well. You feel triggered and notice the same for the other person. You remember this practice and do the following:.

According to recent reports, we all have the tendency to confuse the story we have crafted and are trying to tell with the whole truth about a situation. Perhaps a better way to proceed is to remain open to what we have not yet explored or understood, remain open to another way of thinking about a situation, and remain open to the other person. If we could find the grace to do so, we might learn to see and understand more deeply before we judge. All of this ultimately requires that we develop the courage to question our own certainty. If we could do so, it is very likely that our world would become a much better, kinder place to live and thrive.

Wild turkey feathers can change color

💡 Key Takeaways

  • “Color phases are caused by genetic mutations that affect production of melanin, the pigment that causes the dark coloration in a wild turkey’s plumage,” Michael Chamberlain, National Wild Turkey Federation Endowed Chair, tells Popular Science.
  • There are four general turkey color phases: smokey gray, erythristic, melanistic, and leucistic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as most people in the United States know—especially around this time of the year—wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) are large, broadly dark-colored birds with iridescent feathers and bald necks and heads. But not all turkeys are alike. Some of these boisterous birds have color phases, or non-traditional arrangements in their feathers, or plumage.

“Color phases are caused by genetic mutations that affect production of melanin, the pigment that causes the dark coloration in a wild turkey’s plumage,” Michael Chamberlain, National Wild Turkey Federation Endowed Chair, tells Popular Science.

There are four general turkey color phases: smokey gray, erythristic, melanistic, and leucistic. Smokey gray turkeys don’t have brown pigments in their plumage, and can look white from a distance. Leucistic turkeys have white feathers because they lack melanin production in their plumage, but their heads, beards, and legs appear more normal and red.

Melanistic birds are essentially the opposite. The genetic mutation causes an overproduction of melanin, so the turkey is darker-colored and almost totally black. Erythristic turkeys have an overproduction of carotenoids (types of pigments behind orange, yellow, and red colors) that prevent the production of melanin and also make their feathers more reddish.

In a recent development, how common these different color variations are is still a question, because experts have just started to track their occurrences. Leucistic birds appear to be present throughout North America, while melanistic birds—the completely black ones—seem to be more rare.

“It’s unknown how odd plumage affects survival or reproduction, but it’s logical to assume that lighter colored birds and particularly leucistic and smoke phase birds would be obvious to predators,” explains Chamberlain, who is also known as the Wild Turkey Doc. However, “the relationship between odd plumage and survival or reproduction has never been documented in the literature.”.

In a recent development, but if you come across a picture of a gorgeously-colored bird that looks like a turkey-shaped peacock, chances are that you’re looking at the only other turkey species: the ocellated turkey (Meleagris ocellata). These fantastical looking animals are the wild turkey’s tropical cousin and only exist in the Yucatán Peninsula, and  were domesticated by the ancient Maya.

GLP-1 people have a upcoming symptom to watch for: Sudden vision loss in one eye.

The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) confirmed on November 9 that it will require drugmakers to add information to the warning labels of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and other GLP-1 medications about “a potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).GLP-1 medications are approved to treat type 2 diabetes and to help people lose weight and keep it off.NAION joins a growing list of side effects linked to GLP-1s, adding a second eye warning to several labels.The U.S. labels for Ozempic, Rybelsus, Trulicity, Mounjaro, and Zepbound already warn about diabetic retinopathy, a diabetes-related eye disease, according to each drug’s prescribing information.The two conditions affect different parts of the eye. Diabetic retinopathy damages tiny blood vessels in the retina, the layer at the back of the eye that senses light, according to the National Eye Institute. NAION damages the optic nerve when it doesn’t get enough blood, according to the FDA’s announcement.Mihail Zilbermint, MD, director of endocrine hospitalists at Johns Hopkins, told Healthline he hasn’t seen NAION in his patients. He has seen vision worsen in some people after they start a GLP-1.“But we believe that’s probably related to rapid improvement in their sugar control, which can also be seen in someone who is starting insulin,” Zilbermint noted.

A 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology “initially triggered” the FDA’s review, the agency told Healthline.

The study found a higher risk of NAION in people prescribed semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, than in people prescribed other diabetes or weight-loss drugs.The authors wrote that more research is needed to determine whether semaglutide causes NAION.Joseph F. Rizzo III, MD, director of the Neuro-Ophthalmology Service at Mass Eye and Ear in Boston, served as the study’s corresponding author.

In a recent development, in a 2024 podcast, Rizzo said he and a resident saw three patients with NAION who were taking semaglutide for about a week.“And because NAION is a fairly uncommon disorder in the general population, the fact that we had three within a relatively short period of time led me to suspect that there was a higher risk of developing NAION in patients on semaglutide,” Rizzo said. The FDA analyzed clinical trials for multiple GLP-1 drugs and noted that NAION cases were reported with every GLP-1 on the market, according to its announcement. Those findings led the FDA to require the warning for the entire drug class, the agency told Healthline.

About 70% to 80% of people with NAION first notice vision loss when they wake up, according to StatPearls. The FDA listed these symptoms:.

No treatment has been proven to reverse vision loss from NAION, according to StatPearls.

“Patients experiencing sudden, painless vision loss in one eye should contact their healthcare professional immediately and should not stop their medication without consulting their provider first,” the FDA told Healthline.

In the announcement, the agency told doctors to promptly refer patients with suspected NAION to an ophthalmologist.

The FDA listed these possible risk factors for NAION:.

The FDA told Healthline that many people who take GLP-1s also have these conditions, which made reports of NAION in GLP-1 people “challenging” to interpret.

It has been revealed that across 126 clinical trials, the FDA found about 6 NAION cases per 100,000 people taking a GLP-1 for a year, and about 4 per 100,000 people taking a placebo or another diabetes drug for a year.In real-world data, NAION was more common with GLP-1s than with one type of diabetes pill, but the FDA found no significant increase compared with another type, the agency told Healthline.Zilbermint stated patients who saw the news have worried about losing their vision. He tells them that “many of the serious harms, including the potential harm of NAION, are rare.”“The overall risk is still very small,” he said.

Regulators in other countries have added NAION warnings, mostly for semaglutide:.

The FDA told Healthline the benefits of GLP-1s “continue to outweigh their risks when used as directed.”The FDA has also approved some GLP-1s to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke, reduce the risk of worsening kidney disease, and treat sleep apnea and a type of liver disease.Zilbermint noted that “for most of my patients with obesity, diabetes and heart disease, the benefits clearly outweigh the risks.”“But we definitely have to decide patient by patient,” he added.

The labeling change applies to these medications, according to the FDA’s announcement:.

As of publication, the FDA’s online label database did not yet show the new warning on the drugs’ labels.

#212871. The e-bike industry has a horsepower problem

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (939 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

The e-bike industry has a horsepower problem

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (939 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was a time when 750 watts sounded like a lot of power for an electric bicycle.
  • Recent findings suggest that spend enough time browsing upcoming e-bike releases and you’ll inevitably stumble across bikes advertising 1,000W, 1,500W, 2,000W, or even higher power.
  • If you ask me, the e-bike industry is developing a horsepower problem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was a time when 750 watts sounded like a lot of power for an electric bicycle.

These days, apparently those are rookie numbers.

Recent findings suggest that spend enough time browsing upcoming e-bike releases and you’ll inevitably stumble across bikes advertising 1,000W, 1,500W, 2,000W, or even higher power. Dual-motor models have turned the spec sheet into an arms race, with manufacturers seemingly competing to see who can slap the biggest number onto the product page.

If you ask me, the e-bike industry is developing a horsepower problem.

It has been revealed that to be clear, I’m not anti-power. I’ve ridden everything from dainty 250W European commuter bikes to electric motorcycles with enough power to rearrange your chest cavity. Powerful electric two-wheelers are fun, period.

But there’s a difference between building a powerful electric two-wheeler and pretending that every powerful electric two-wheeler is still an electric bicycle.

In the US, the widely adopted three-class e-bike system generally tops out at 20 mph (32 km/h) for Class 1 and Class 2 e-bikes and 28 mph (45 km/h) for Class 3, with some minor exceptions, and 750 watts has long been a common benchmark for the motor power limit.

Yet browse online e-bike retailers today and you’ll find plenty of machines advertised with motors well beyond that figure, often capable of speeds far beyond normal electric bicycle classifications.

Sometimes there’s a disclaimer explaining that the bike is intended for “off-road use.” Sometimes there’s a software setting that supposedly limits it for street riding.

And sometimes people just sort of squint at the pedals and agree to keep calling it an electric bicycle.

The problem isn’t that 2,000W electric two-wheelers exist. I love lightweight electric motorcycles and mopeds, or what some are beginning to refer to as ‘e-motos’, despite that terminology having its own concerns. So sure, those bikes are great and there is a time and place for such power. The problem is that the industry increasingly seems afraid to call them what they are.

Part of the blame belongs to consumers – to us.

According to recent reports, E-bike shopping has become increasingly spec-sheet driven, and wattage provides an incredibly easy number to compare. If ‘Bike A’ has a 750W motor and ‘Bike B’ costs the same but advertises 1,500W, it’s easy to assume ‘Bike B’ is twice as good. This is especially true for younger riders who lack a deeper understanding of how e-bikes work, and just want something powerful and fast to impress their friends after school. They beg their parents for the latest models with the biggest motors, and many parents give in.

The problem is that’s not how electric bikes work – there’s so much more to a bike than the motor wattage rating.

According to recent reports, motor design, controller current, battery voltage, thermal management, gearing, efficiency and software tuning all influence performance. A beautifully tuned 500W or 750W system can be far nicer to ride – and sometimes more useful – than a poorly implemented motor advertising twice the power.

It has been revealed that but “excellent controller tuning” doesn’t look nearly as exciting in a giant font on an Amazon listing. So manufacturers respond rationally based on what consumers demand: They make the number bigger.

The result is an e-bike horsepower war that is ultimately hurting the entire industry.

Industry observers note that when riders blast through bike paths on motorcycle-performance machines marketed as “e-bikes,” pedestrians don’t care whether the motor technically arrived in a street-legal mode. Police officers aren’t going to inspect controller settings. And lawmakers aren’t famous for approaching emerging transportation technology with surgical precision.

They see a fast machine with pedals, hear complaints about dangerous “e-bikes,” and start writing laws that affect everyone – including riders on perfectly ordinary commuter e-bikes.

In my opinion, that’s the part that should worry anyone who enjoys riding an e-bike.

In Germany cops inspect controller settings on e-bikes and scooters all the time and also do practical tests - they just get on the bike/scooter and manually test what max speed can it reach. If it exceeds the legal limit and does not carry the required paperwork for that - it gets confiscated on the spot at whoever drove it gets a fine and points on their license (even if they don't have one yet).

Sources indicate that there’s absolutely a place for high-powered electric two-wheelers. In fact, I want more of them. Lightweight electric mopeds and motorcycles could replace an enormous number of car trips while using a fraction of the energy and space. Those are highly capable machines, but they need to be used appropriately, registered legally, and ridden responsibly.

And we don’t help that cause by pretending they’re bicycles.

Perhaps the e-bike industry’s next great innovation doesn’t need another 500 watts.

Industry observers note that maybe it just needs a little more honesty about what we’re actually building. So let’s build more electric bicycles. And yes, let’s build more e-motos and electric motorcycles. But let’s not confuse the two, either.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A well-known ancient Egyptian curse is not only older than historians thought—the curse that called upon the sun god’s wrath upon one’s enemies was much more commonly employed than experts assumed. However, the new evidence concerning the “Apophis ritual” wasn’t recently discovered in an excavated spellbook. According to a study published in the Journal of the Egyptian Language and Antiquities, archaeologists learned the latest details from postage stamp-sized papyrus fragments left in 3,400-year-old trash piles.

In a recent development, prior to finding the 40 charred remnants, the only documentation of the Apophis ritual was a ritual manual dating back to the late fourth century BCE. Egyptian priests originally designed the spell to aid the sun god Ra against Apophis, his eternal foe and the snake god of chaos, fire, and darkness. Others later adapted the ritual to curse enemies of the pharaoh and counter problems associated with the serpent like inclement weather and poisons. But although researchers initially assumed the Apophis ritual was reserved for religious leaders, the papyrus fragments retrieved from temple ruins at Thebes have dramatically expanded its audience.

Sources indicate that “They show that the ritual was much older than the one surviving copy from the fourth century [BCE] might suggest,” Fredrik Hagen, an Egyptologist at the University of Copenhagen and study co-author, remarked in a statement. “Already 1,000 years earlier, during what we call the Fresh Kingdom, it was an integrated part of Egyptian culture.”.

While additional analysis of the fragments revealed that such rituals were widespread in ancient Egypt, Hagen explained that additional contextual references to the Apophis incantation indicate it was a “common feature” in daily life.

“We know that literate people, including those who were not priests, had access to magical rituals and functioned as magicians and healers,” he said. “It is clear that people approached scribes for help in performing magic, both for protection and for attacking others.”.

Recent findings suggest that the existence of the remnants are surprising in their own right, given what the ritual required. Their charring is only part of the necessary curse protocols—prior to burning the written spells, practitioners stepped on the papyrus, stabbed it with a knife, and even spit on it.

“For the ritual to be successful, the materials had to be destroyed by fire, so we are extremely fortunate to have found any of them in a condition that still allows them to be recognized and studied,” said Hagen.

#212869. Should Scientists Ignore Philosophers of Science?

Should Scientists Ignore Philosophers of Science?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.
  • The eminent evolutionary biologist and modeller John Maynard Smith was once asked about Karl Popper and the philosophy of science.
  • Recent findings suggest that this is why I've recently published an academic article on the topic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.

The eminent evolutionary biologist and modeller John Maynard Smith was once asked about Karl Popper and the philosophy of science. His answer was not flattering. His impression was that scientists who take the philosophy of science seriously, and allow their research to be influenced by philosophical preconceptions, are "far more likely to do themselves harm than good". He loved reading philosophy of science and was always ready to argue about it, he added, but he did not believe that one should allow oneself to be influenced by it when actually thinking about science.

Recent findings suggest that this is why I've recently published an academic article on the topic. These are quite radical words, and though Maynard Smith's generalisation is untenable, there is an notable insight to be extracted.

If modellers approach the philosophical literature on models with the goal of figuring out what models are and what a good model is, they might easily find themselves lured into naive monistic views of models that fail to represent the full epistemic richness of modelling practices, thereby turning them into worse scientists than they could have otherwise been.

Sources indicate that this could happen in several ways. For instance, models with epistemic functions not recognised by narrow monist accounts might be discarded. Consider, for example, models with weak predictive power, but great generality and insight into complex systems.

According to recent reports, perhaps Maynard Smith's worry is most strongly illustrated in economics, where Milton Friedman and Karl Popper are taken to have the "last word" in any methodological debate, and are frequently invoked to both defend and criticise the work of modellers. They are perhaps paradigm cases of monist thinking. Friedman argued that the only relevant desideratum in science concerns predictive power, while Popper argued that what matters is falsifiability.

These accounts of science have received extensive criticism over the last decades. Indeed, the philosopher Alex Rosenberg argued that Friedman's naive picture single-handedly justified the existence of philosophy of economics as a distinct profession. Economists, however, are unlikely to read much if any work on methodology beyond Friedman and Popper. As the economist Dani Rodrik notes, economic methodology is relegated to specialised journals and, more importantly, is not really being taught in graduate school.

The result is that economists seem to believe that their science operates according to a simple form of falsificationism, a picture of science that, most contemporary philosophers of science would agree, both misrepresents scientific practice and provides the wrong ideal of how science ought to function.

The obvious counter to Maynard Smith's concern is that it is not an argument against the philosophy of science, but rather against bad philosophy of science, which limits, rather than fosters, insights into the richness of the epistemic tools available to scientists.

Industry observers note that philosophers are not innocent here. Some debates in the philosophy of science rest on such monist motivations to seek univocal accounts of laws, explanation, species, functions, preferences, and many more. As Peter Godfrey-Smith emphasised, one of the hazards of philosophy is the temptation to come up with theories that are "too broad and sweeping". This hazard has not been avoided in the philosophical literature on models. Many philosophers of science seem to be under the impression that once we figure out what "models" are and how they work, we can finally get a handle on all the other pressing questions in the philosophy of science. I argue that this way of thinking about models is grounded in a mistake.

Industry observers note that A philosophy of science worth reading takes the plurality, diversity, and richness of models and modelling practices seriously. It does not hand scientists a single criterion for good science.

In a recent development, economists, Rodrik argues, need a better story about the kind of science they practise, and some economists have recently engaged with philosophical questions themselves, seeking contact with philosophers of economics in the process. Philosophers of science, in turn, should turn more of their attention toward both the social sciences and the philosophy of the social sciences. Their lack of engagement with this rich literature is a historical omission that may have provided a misguided understanding of how science works.

Sources indicate that should scientists ignore philosophers? They should ignore those who tell them that there is only one way of doing science well.

1 in 3 Infants Diagnosed With Peanut Allergy May Not Have the Condition

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (925 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.
  • According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.
  • However, new research published in the November 2026 concern of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.

According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.

However, new research published in the November 2026 concern of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.

In fact, having a history of reacting to peanuts and positive allergy testing on their own may not be sufficient to diagnose a peanut allergy for many infants.

The study’s authors suggest that a threshold oral food challenge — in which the child is given increasing amounts of the suspected food allergen under medical supervision to look for an allergic reaction — should be routinely considered to help confirm peanut allergy.

This additional testing could safely prevent children who are not allergic to peanuts from undergoing unnecessary treatment with oral immunotherapy.

It could also spare families from burdensome food restrictions and allergy precautions.

The researchers’ goal was to evaluate the accuracy and safety of the Allergy Development to an Accelerated Path to Tolerance (ADAPT) peanut oral immunotherapy program, which was established in 2024 at 10 public children’s hospitals across Australia.

This program provides a standardized approach to evaluating and treating infants with suspected peanut allergies.

The study included infants who had experienced a mild to moderate reaction to peanut before 12 months of age and had evidence of peanut sensitization through allergy testing.

Researchers reviewed medical records to examine how accurately the program’s approach identified peanut allergies and whether it could safely guide treatment.

According to recent reports, A key part of the evaluation was a threshold oral food challenge. The challenge involved up to seven doses, ranging from 15 to 1,300 milligrams of peanut protein.

Medical teams monitored the infants for reactions and provided treatment when necessary.

Researchers reviewed records from April 2024 through October 2025. During that period, 1,275 infants were assessed through the program, and 778 underwent an oral food challenge.

The researchers also examined allergy test results and whether infants who reacted during the challenges could begin oral immunotherapy at an appropriate starting dose.

At the time of the oral food challenge, the infants had a median age of 13 months.

Of the 778 infants who underwent an oral food challenge, 507 (65.2%) had an allergic reaction.

However, 271 (34.8%) did not react to peanut during the supervised test, despite having a history of a previous reaction and positive allergy test results.

These findings suggest that relying on medical history and allergy tests alone may lead some infants to be labeled with a peanut allergy when they can actually tolerate the food.

According to recent reports, among the infants who reacted during the challenges, 61 experienced anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction that can affect breathing and blood pressure. This represented 12% of infants with a positive challenge and 7.8% of all infants who underwent testing. Medical teams safely managed these severe allergic reactions.

Researchers also found that infants who reacted to peanut generally had higher skin prick test results and Ara h 2-specific IgE levels than those who did not react.

However, these test results did not reliably indicate how much peanut would trigger a reaction or how severe that reaction would be.

Of the 394 infants who began peanut oral immunotherapy, 384 (97.5%) successfully started treatment at a dose below the amount that had triggered a reaction during their food challenge.

The researchers say these findings support considering supervised oral food challenges to confirm suspected peanut allergies before starting treatment or recommending long-term avoidance.

Erin Banta, MD, a board certified allergist and immunologist who treats both children and adults at Latitude Food Allergy Care in Great Neck, Newly introduced York, said these findings are significant because they provide evidence for early use of oral food challenges in infants with peanut reactions.

“In those with mild-moderate prior reactions to peanut, early oral food challenge may allow for either delabeling of food allergy (in 1/3 of the patients in this study) or diagnosis of food allergy,” she told Healthline.

Banta, who wasn’t involved in the study, added that early delabeling takes a significant burden off the patient and their family.

“On the other hand,” she explained, “early diagnosis allows for early initiation of treatment with oral immunotherapy at a time in the patient’s life associated with the greatest success rates.”.

Banta further noted that the study offers different pathways for oral immunotherapy based on the patient’s reaction threshold. This means that some patients may be able to complete treatment more rapidly due to their individual threshold dose.

Lindsey Forstie, FNP, a family nurse practitioner with clinical training and experience in allergy and asthma care at Carefree Allergy in Phoenix, AZ, added that while further evaluation may be needed to confirm a peanut allergy diagnosis, it’s important for parents not to try introducing peanuts at home.

“Instead, they should speak with their pediatrician or allergist about appropriate testing and whether a supervised food challenge is safe and necessary,” she said.

According to Forstie, who was also not part of the study, the goal is to avoid unnecessary food restrictions while also keeping children safe.

Sources indicate that “The key message is that not every positive allergy test means a child has a food allergy,” she told Healthline. “Accurate diagnosis helps protect children while allowing those who are not allergic to enjoy a more normal, less restrictive diet.”.

Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.
