Industry News: Meteorites fascinated ancient Egyptians—just look at King Tut’s ‘space dagger’

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1334 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in August 2026, an analysis of iron from ancient Greek tombs revealed surprising results.
  • It seems that, among the upper classes of Bronze Age Greece, rings fashioned from this out-of-this-world metal were all the rage.
  • Researchers believe that the Greek meteoric rings were actually imported from Egypt: a land with a special relationship to this metal from the skies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in August 2026, an analysis of iron from ancient Greek tombs revealed surprising results. The objects surveyed included weapons and jewelry from around 3,000 to 4,000 years ago. Most of them were fashioned from regular old iron ore, but around 10 rings were made of iron from outer space—aka from meteorites that crash-landed on Earth.

It seems that, among the upper classes of Bronze Age Greece, rings fashioned from this out-of-this-world metal were all the rage. Before people learned how to extract iron from ore by melting it at super-high temperatures—a process called smelting—the only source of metallic iron was the occasional space rock. This material, known as meteoric iron, is rare worldwide, but especially in Greece, where approaching meteors usually disappear into the sea rather than make landfall.

Researchers believe that the Greek meteoric rings were actually imported from Egypt: a land with a special relationship to this metal from the skies.

Industry observers note that meteoric iron can be identified because it’s purer than the iron ore that naturally occurs on Earth, with a higher proportion of nickel mixed into it. Because meteoric iron “already arrives on Earth in metallic form,” states Victoria Almansa-Villatoro, a professor of Egyptology at Yale University, “it’s very malleable” and can be shaped more easily than unrefined ore.

Industry observers note that the Egyptians started working with this rare material early. “The oldest meteoric iron objects in the world come from Egypt,” says Almansa-Villatoro: Nine small beads, excavated from a site called Gerzeh along the bank of the Nile about 20 miles south of Cairo, are the oldest artifacts discovered made from space rocks. They are dated to around 3,200 BCE, more than a thousand years older than the 10 meteoric iron rings found in Greece.

Not only are the Gerzeh beads older than any other meteoric iron objects, they are much, much older than widespread iron smelting in Egypt. Almansa-Villatoro explains that “Egypt was relatively late in comparison with other Near Eastern civilizations to start smelting iron.” By the time the Egyptians were producing iron on a large scale in the 500s BCE, ancient people in Anatolia and other regions had been doing it for about five hundred years.

A major reason for this late adoption was Egypt’s natural resources. Iron smelting forges burned a lot of wood charcoal, and Egypt had no large forests. For centuries, the Egyptians relied on bronze, which cost less fuel to produce. It wasn’t until major changes in political and trade networks, including pressure to match the iron arsenals of foreign enemies like the Assyrians, that the Egyptians finally made the shift.

In a recent development, while early iron weapons and armor were not automatically better than bronze ones, iron proved easier to repair, and could be strengthened through further reworking. But objects like the Gerzeh beads show that the ancient Egyptians shaped small amounts of meteoric iron long before they knew how to extract it from ore.

The Gerzeh iron beads were incorporated into jewelry with gems and gold, hinting at their perceived value. All of the other Egyptian objects believed to be made of meteoric iron are similarly small and mostly decorative. The largest and most spectacular is a dagger with a meteoric iron blade more than eight inches long. It was found in the tomb of Egypt’s famous pharaoh, Tutankhamun, who died around 1,323 BCE.

Government records from the reign of Tutankhamun’s grandfather, Amenhotep III, mention an Anatolian king gifting a dagger to the Pharaoh. “People have speculated that this was the same dagger,” says Almansa-Villatoro. “Because, why would they make such a big deal about this king receiving a dagger from a foreign leader, unless it’s made of a very crucial or very rare material?” As seen with the recent findings from Greece, demand for meteoric iron in the ancient Mediterranean was international.

As of 2013, archaeologists had discovered 28 objects in Egypt believed to be made of meteoric iron. This accounts for about half of the 55 known ancient meteoric iron artifacts found across Europe, Asia, and Africa as of 2023.

The prevalence of meteoric iron in Egypt is difficult to determine, as the composition of many iron objects has never been evaluated. Additionally, indicates Almansa-Villatoro, “we find more things in Egypt in general from this time period than in other regions,” due to the long history of archaeology there.

Analysis has shown that some of the Egyptian meteoric iron objects are made from several small meteorites combined. This might suggest that the Egyptians were “harvesting” and “actively looking” for this rare material, says Almansa-Villatoro, rather than just using it at random when a meteorite happened to land nearby.

Almansa-Villatoro believes that meteoric iron “was valuable because it was recognized to be material that came from the sky,” not just because it was more pure than other iron. Ancient Egyptian religious texts link iron with the heavens and the spiritual realm of the gods, who were sometimes described as having iron bones. One Egyptian term for iron literally translates to “the iron of the sky.“.

According to recent reports, “Some tools made of meteoric iron were used in a very crucial funerary ritual known as ‘the Opening of the Mouth,’” says Almansa-Villatoro. These include small iron blades found in Tutankhamun’s tomb (though not the famous dagger). The purpose of this ritual was “to give the deceased back their senses,” Almansa-Villatoro explains, allowing them to speak, breathe, and eat in the afterlife. Meteoric iron might have been particularly prized for crafting these ritual objects.

By the time of Tutankhamun’s reign, the Egyptians might have encountered smelted iron produced in other lands, but they were still using meteoric iron in rituals and reverently placing it in tombs.

“It is possible that they still saw meteoric iron as something different” from smelted iron, claims Almansa-Villatoro, though it’s hard to say for sure.

Ancient Greece’s most famous oracle was just high on gas fumes.

In medieval France, murderous pigs faced trial and execution.

Ancient Romans thought drinking gladiator blood could cure epilepsy.

At Scotland’s ancient Cladh Hallan, homes were full of human bones.

7 ways toilets have killed people.

For ancient Romans, pooping was a group activity.

Some Egyptian texts describe a dome of water with an iron shell enclosing the Earth. Meteoric iron might have been explained as fragments of this cosmic shell breaking off and falling to the Earth.

Recent findings suggest that it’s clear that the Egyptians considered meteoric iron to be a special material, but what exactly they knew or didn’t know about it is not always easy to figure out. The Egyptians understood and interpreted the world around them using very different methods from our own. While we rely on experimental data documented in writing, ancient Egypt “was very much an oral society, where knowledge was transmitted through ritual and through recitation of texts,” says Almansa-Villatoro.

Recent findings suggest that in ancient Egypt, “things that we wouldn’t consider science nowadays, like myth, could have fulfilled the same function” as science does today, says Almansa-Villatoro. The Egyptians used narrative myths to describe the physical universe. The iron shell surrounding the Earth appears in accounts of the soul’s journey to the afterlife, as a barrier that the spirits of the dead must sail across to reach the skies.

In a recent development, with our modern knowledge, it’s easy to explain how a space rock might land on Earth. But what if all you knew of outer space was what you could see with your eyes from our planet’s surface? Egyptian myths may not have the structure of a modern scientific paper, but they offer a glimpse into how ancient people made sense of awe-inspiring natural phenomena like metal falling from the skies.

#212755. Tech Report: How to Rapidly Weed Out Manipulators When Dating

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1004 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: How to Rapidly Weed Out Manipulators When Dating

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1004 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The dating world is full of tricksters.
  • Ordinarily, empathy is what allows you to remain close to the people that you care about.
  • According to recent reports, however, in the dating world, some people may have a victim mentality.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Lybi Ma.

The dating world is full of tricksters. If you are a person with emotional intelligence, several of your EI tendencies may backfire with a certain type of person. This may be especially true when your heart is involved and you long to be loved. Four EI qualities can work against you when you are dating; empathy, perspective-taking, vulnerability, and positivity. Educating yourself on how and when to rein them in may help you quickly weed out a manipulator.

Ordinarily, empathy is what allows you to remain close to the people that you care about. You open your heart and your mind to better understand them. Thinking about how they must feel in their situation allows you to resonate and really “feel for them.” When you convey this understanding to them, they usually feel less alone, connected to you because you get it, and a bit better. It can be transformative.

According to recent reports, however, in the dating world, some people may have a victim mentality. They believe that their life has been harder than anyone else’s and they identify a list of past hardships to elicit your empathy. Yet, instead of integrating your empathy to gain emotional relief, they indirectly invite you to “fix” things for them. Often this requires that you sacrifice something that is crucial to you.

Although you think that they are opening up when they tell you their tales of woe, they may not be. A person with a victim narrative rarely talks about how they grappled with difficult and nuanced emotions to recover. Nor do they identify any profound insight or a silver lining. This may signify that they did not actually recover from their past difficulties but rather prefer to use them to dodge accountability in a current relationship, so be careful. The sad narratives can result in you feeling like their life has been harder than yours, so you must give more to them and the relationship. Yet, after a while, you realize that you are being exploited.

According to recent reports, it is vital to note that you too have been through your share of trauma. However, if you have emotional intelligence, you are someone who can recognize, identify, and process deep and uncomfortable emotions. Your self-awareness and ability to deeply reflect on your experiences allow you to eventually recover, grow, and become stronger. A person who lacks these abilities tends to use their past difficulties as a license to manipulate others in the present.

If you are someone who possesses emotional intelligence, you also look at different perspectives without even recognizing that you are. It’s almost automatic. Your desire to truly understand the people that you care about drives you to look at things from their viewpoint. Unfortunately, there are many people in the dating world who do not take perspective. It can be deceiving because their unwavering belief that they are always right in the context of their interpersonal relationships makes them appear uber confident. Yet, this may not be the case. This individual may be too insecure to be wrong, so they refuse to look at things from your angle. They continually espouse their viewpoint as correct and dismiss and ignore your opinion about the matter. This can create an imbalance of power in the relationship because you are always trying to understand their perspective, and they rarely consider yours. To avoid the disagreements that this unfairness creates, you often acquiesce and continually surrender to what they say and want. As the relationship progresses, they gain more and more emotional control over you.

Sources indicate that as an EI person, your vulnerability is normally a strength because you are secure enough to truly open up to someone new, but it can backfire with a problematic person. Since you are not defensive or emotionally walled off, you are comfortable talking about your insecurities, uncomfortable emotions, scars, fears, and idiosyncrasies. In fact, you long for closeness and are excited at the thought of becoming close with someone new. However, if you don’t keep an eye on this tendency at the beginning of a relationship, you may open up too soon and with too much personal and private information.

According to recent reports, if your date is a problematic person, they may use this data to hurt you during an argument. They may also weaponize it to zap your confidence because they want you to feel “small” so they feel “big.” This creates another type of imbalance in the relationship because their self-narrative is absent of any deep and emotional self-disclosures. They simply describe a litany of hardships. So, now they know all of your insecurities, but you know none of theirs. To add insult to injury, they may glibly reference a general insecurity to excuse a wrongdoing or to exploit your empathy.

Industry observers note that lastly, as an EI person, you tend to see the good in people. You are a glass-half-full individual, and you long for harmony and good vibes in your relationships-- and this is a remarkable quality in most situations. However, when you are in the dating world, it can cause problems. Your positivity can tempt you to dismiss a latest person’s red flags and thoughtless behaviors, which can create inequality in the relationship. You are “all in,” and you give as much as possible to this person while they give far less, emotionally, and are very critical of you.

Everyone is on their best behavior at the beginning of a dating relationship, so do not give a new person too much credit too early. Be aware of your emotionally intelligent tendencies and rein them in when you need to.

You can find more information on this topic in my book, How to Outsmart a Narcissist: Use Emotional Intelligence to Regain Control at Home, at Work, and In Life.

In a recent development, the next time you hit the slopes, you might see one of ChargePoint’s EV chargers either in the ski resort’s parking lot or directly at the base of the ski run. That’s because the charging network and electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) manufacturer has partnered with Kässbohrer, the maker of the iconic PistenBully slope groomer.

Effective immediately, the partnership puts Kässbohrer’s clients, which range from ski resort operators to public parking operators, in direct contact with ChargePoint, which builds the hardware and software for its EV charging network.

As a result, ski resorts and indoor ski facilities can get access to an entire charging ecosystem for electric snow groomers and other electric vehicles that may be in a tech giant’s fleet.

"Electrification is reaching heavy-duty vehicles that operate under some of the toughest conditions anywhere," said John Saffrett, EVP and Managing Director, Europe at ChargePoint. "Kässbohrer is trusted by ski resorts and fleet operators around the world. Together, we're helping customers electrify entire operations, from snow groomers to public parking, while reducing emissions, improving energy management, and lowering operating costs.".

In a recent development, as luck would have it, Kässbohrer happens to build an all-electric snow groomer, so the partnership goes both ways. ChargePoint gets to sell more chargers, while Kässbohrer gets to sell more electric snow groomers.

The PistenBully 100 E packs a massive 196-kilowatt-hour battery pack rated at 800 volts, which enables a three-hour runtime for the 7-tonne tracked EV. That’s adequate for small to moderately long ski slopes, but for longer slopes, a quick recharge may be needed, and here’s where ChargePoint’s expertise comes into play.

According to Kässbohrer, the first-ever electric PistenBully can accept up to 150 kW from a DC fast charger, with roughly one hour needed to get the battery from zero to full. With its 268-horsepower, 10,939-pound-foot electric powertrain, the 100 E can drive at up to 17 miles per hour.

"With the PistenBully 100 E, emission-free slope grooming has arrived on the mountain, remarked Tim Estelmann, Product Manager at Kässbohrer. “But for it to function reliably and sustainably, the right infrastructure is essential. Only when the vehicle and charging solution work together does a powerful machine become a system that operators can rely on day after day and night after night. That is precisely why we are partnering with ChargePoint, together creating the foundation for long-term operational efficiency and sustainability.".

Sources indicate that kässbohrer also sells a series hybrid diesel-electric snow groomer that pairs a Cummins oil burner with two electric motors. The diesel engine acts as a generator, so it can keep the revs lower compared to conventional diesel snow groomers. According to Kässbohrer, the PistenBully 600 E+ has up to 20% lower carbon dioxide emissions, up to 20% lower fuel consumption, and is 20% quieter than conventional snow preparation machines.

According to ChargePoint, over half of the snow groomers sold worldwide each year are made by Kässbohrer, so there’s plenty of room to grow for both companies.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in 1941, General Motors hit the open road with its fleet of Futureliners on the Parade of Progress, a movement meant to spread cutting-edge science and technology across America. With their bubble-top cockpits, exhibition-style innards, and shining chrome panels, the Futureliners became as much of a spectacle as the displays on automotive technology, urban engineering, farming, and leisure pursuits carried within. Now, 85 years later, a resurrected Futureliner is carrying the Parade of Progress torch into the 21st Century—starting in Upcoming York City.

Industry observers note that like many modern automotive stories, this Futureliner's resurrection began on Facebook Marketplace. When Matt Katz, owner of the Caretakers Collection, was sent a link to an available Futureliner on the online classified site, he jumped into action. Katz was on the phone with the seller in a matter of minutes, and swiftly deputized friend and Fresh Jersey car builder Rob Ida to travel up to Massachusetts the following day.

“[The seller] was totally caught off guard that I just called him. He's like, ‘Listen, like it's Monday night. I'm out at an event. You know, call me tomorrow.’ I'm like, ‘No, no, no, I want to make this deal now.’ I just wanted to lock it up,” Katz said to Road & Track. He said he informed the seller that he wanted Ida, with whom Katz had done prior restoration projects, to come check out the Futureliner. “I was like, ‘Let me call [Ida] and get him to come out and inspect it within forty-eight hours. And if all is good, I'll wire you the balance. And if all is not, return the money to me, the deposit, and we'll call it even.’”.

Ida reported back that the Futureliner example was ripe for restoration, but the journey couldn’t begin immediately. First, Ida had to cut a larger opening in his garage to fit the Futureliner through. Standing 11-feet-7-inches tall and 33 feet long, the GM Futureliner is taller than your average school bus, and about as long as an average fire truck. But once the Futureliner had been transported and maneuvered into Ida’s garage, the real work began.

As it had been owned and restored by the Peter Pan Bus Organization in the 1990s, this Futureliner build started out in better shape than most. It had been updated with GM’s post-World War II styling from 1953—a flatter and less regal version of the shape introduced in 1939. Ida and Katz wanted to bring this Futureliner back to its original Harley Earl-designed glory, but there wasn’t an official blueprint to guide them. Ida even reached out to the General Motors Heritage Center, but it had limited information available about the first-generation Futureliner design. So, Ida had to fabricate many of the parts himself. Some era-specific parts even required the creation of bespoke molds, as no replacements were available.

According to recent reports, “We work off imagery, and we work off of any kind of text or information that we can find. Unfortunately, the Thirty-Nine version is much more difficult to find than the Fifty-Three version. Anytime you do a quick search, you're going to find all the white roof Fifty-Three generation-two post-war Futureliner. So that was really the difficult part: digging deep enough to find the Thirty-Nine version,” Ida said to Road & Track.

Industry observers note that “Somewhere in a conversation with Rob, it came to be that we both agreed: let's go back to the bubble. Let's bring it back to Thirty-Nine, and we didn't realize and truly fully appreciate what that meant. Getting the bubble done was just difficult, but we knew what to do, and Rob had experience,” Katz stated. “We didn't realize that after we made that decision, everything else would change on the bus. Not just the paint colors, but also the cladding on the side. So, Fifty-Three has seven clads; ours is four. The GM logo on the front. Rob randomly found this old video by a production tech giant called Rose that I discovered, and he poured through it and discovered in a small clip that the GM logo was backlit.”.

In a recent development, once the restoration was complete, Katz and Ida were eager to show off the piece of moving history, and the inaugural Retromobile event in Upcoming York City was the perfect venue. But the newly revived Futureliner had to make it from Old Bridge, New Jersey, to Manhattan’s Jacob K. Javits Convention Center. There is no shortage of driving obstacles between those two points on a good day in a regular car, so piloting the massive machine was sure to be a challenge—but with Ida and Katz at the helm, however, the journey went smoother than expected. Thanks to dually-style front wheels, power steering, 360-degree cameras, and working air conditioning, driving the Futureliner was an exercise in patience more than anything else.

“So I drove from Columbus Circle to Times Square to Javits. And as a Latest Yorker, driving it in New York and just seeing people's reactions ... you know, part of the enjoyment is how people react to it. I've never had a reaction like when I was driving it. And then the fact that they closed Times Square for me while we were driving, and for Rob and me ... I couldn't even have fathomed that as a dream,” Katz stated.

In a recent development, and the Futureliner’s adventures are far from over. Katz and Ida are presently scheming a cross-country road trip, starting on the East Coast in 2027 and heading west toward GM’s Heritage Center in Sterling, Michigan. After that, the Futureliner will head to California for the 2027 Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance, with stops at dealerships and historical markers along the way. The Futureliner will then spend some time at the Petersen Automotive Museum in Los Angeles and stick around for the 2028 Summer Olympics before heading back to GM’s Heritage Center. This cross-country journey will be focused on charity efforts for organizations like the Sloan Kettering Institute for Cancer Research, which the original Parade of Progress highlighted. Trust us: if the Futureliner comes to your town, it’s worth seeing in person.

A New York transplant hailing from the Pacific Northwest, Emmet White has a passion for anything that goes: cars, bicycles, planes, and motorcycles. After learning to ride at 17, Emmet worked in the motorcycle industry before joining Autoweek in 2022 and Road & Track in 2024. The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The EREV is Toyota’s fifth “electrified” vehicle, a term that now spans pure electric vehicles (EVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), hybrids (HEVs), and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).
  • Unlike fully electric vehicles, an EREV also uses a gas engine that serves as a generator to recharge the battery when it gets low, thereby extending the driving range.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is set to reveal its first extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) on November 27, and from the first look, it could be based on its flagship Highlander SUV.

The EREV is Toyota’s fifth “electrified” vehicle, a term that now spans pure electric vehicles (EVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), hybrids (HEVs), and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).

Unlike fully electric vehicles, an EREV also uses a gas engine that serves as a generator to recharge the battery when it gets low, thereby extending the driving range.

In a recent development, EREVs use a smaller battery than a pure electric vehicle, while the engine is typically smaller than a PHEV. While they are quieter and often cheaper than a plug-in, EREVs are also less efficient than a pure EV.

A Nikkei report in September claimed that Toyota was preparing to begin production of its first EREV in China in Spring 2027.

It appears the rumors are true. Toyota’s joint venture in China, GAC Toyota, posted a preview on its Weibo account with the caption #Toyota doesn’t rush but range-extended.

Recent findings suggest that toyota didn’t confirm the name, but all signs point to it being the Highlander EREV. The blurry preview looks like the Highlander, and when translated into English, a part of the text below it reads “Cash in on the classics. Global flagship SUV. Not a quick fix, but a range extender.”.

GAC Toyota will reveal the newly introduced EREV at the Guangzhou Motor Show on November 27. Check back for the full details.

According to recent reports, according to the Nikkei report, Toyota aims to produce 200,000 EREVs in 2027. In 2028, it expects production to double to around 400,000 units.

While Toyota likely won’t bring the extended-range EV to the US, it is set to launch the fully electric version of its three-row Highlander in early 2027 (shown above on the left).

The all-electric Toyota Highlander BEV will be available with front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive powertrains with two battery packs: 77 kWh or 95.8 kWh. The smaller (77 kWh) battery provides up to 287 miles of range, while the larger (95.8 kWh) battery provides up to 320 miles in FWD models.

Inside, the electric Toyota Highlander EV offers three rows of seating with room for up to seven passengers.

The three-row electric SUV will be built at Toyota’s manufacturing plant in Georgetown, Kentucky.

Like most foreign brands, Toyota is struggling to keep up with domestic brands like BYD, Geely, and Chery in China’s brutal auto market.

However, it’s Toyota’s gas and hybrid cars that are getting crushed by the competition. In the first nine months of 2026, Toyota sold just over 1.05 million vehicles in China, about 19% fewer than in the same period last year.

After sales plunged nearly 20%, marking its eighth consecutive month with lower year-over-year sales, Toyota mentioned the market in China “remained weak due in part to rising gasoline prices, while the market for gasoline vehicles and hybrid vehicles was particularly affected.”.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, BYD introduces a self-driving SUV with 600 miles of range that recharges in 10 minutes. These guys are toast.

In a recent development, toyota looks to avoid the intensifying price war with pure electric vehicles in China. An EREV can potentially be offered at a premium, especially as a flagship SUV.

A organization executive said (via Nikkei) that “Competition in China is intensifying as the market fixates on battery EVs, leading to price wars among automakers,” adding, “We need to take steps to avoid being dragged into that competition.”.

Will an EREV help power Toyota’s comeback in China? Or is it late to the party once again? Share your thoughts in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that GLP-1 medications have transformed obesity and type 2 diabetes treatment.
  • A comprehensive new review published on November 5 in the journal Science evaluated the current evidence on how GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide may affect the brain across aging, cardiometabolic disease, and Alzheimer’s disease.
  • Sources indicate that the authors of the review suggested that GLP-1 medications like Ozempic and Zepbound may offer brain health benefits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that GLP-1 medications have transformed obesity and type 2 diabetes treatment. Now, researchers are investigating whether the effects of this blockbuster class of drugs extend beyond weight loss and affect brain health.

A comprehensive new review published on November 5 in the journal Science evaluated the current evidence on how GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide may affect the brain across aging, cardiometabolic disease, and Alzheimer’s disease.

Sources indicate that the authors of the review suggested that GLP-1 medications like Ozempic and Zepbound may offer brain health benefits. However, they were also left with the question of whether the medications act directly on the brain or whether better brain health is actually a consequence of improved cardiometabolic health.

Sheena Aurora, MD, vice president, Medical Affairs, Alzheimer’s Association, who wasn’t involved in the review, told Healthline that more research is needed to better understand the effects of GLP-1 drugs on the brain.

“While research suggests GLP-1s could reduce brain inflammation, improve blood vessel health, and even protect neurons, much broader, randomized clinical trials on GLP-1s and brain health, including in people with Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias, are needed,” she mentioned.

Sources indicate that GLP-1 medications like semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, mimic the GLP-1 hormone. Tirzepatide, the active ingredient in Mounjaro and Zepbound, also targets a second hormone pathway called GIP.

These medications have been shown to produce significant weight loss and improvements in cardiometabolic health.

In a recent development, this is important for brain health because obesity, type 2 diabetes, and vascular dysfunction are all linked with cognitive impairment and dementia. Insulin resistance and chronic inflammation may also link metabolic and brain health.

According to recent reports, analyses of large outcome trials and observational cohorts have suggested that GLP-1 medications may be associated with a reduced risk of cognitive impairment and dementia. However, randomized trials in diseases like Alzheimer’s disease have yet to demonstrate clinical benefits.

Around 200 preclinical and mechanistic studies have shown benefits for learning, memory, synaptic plasticity, and neuronal resilience, though results are heterogeneous in design and direction, so a clear consensus on magnitude and mechanism remains lacking.

It is also unclear how well GLP-1 medications reach the brain. They appear to reach certain areas, such as the hypothalamus, brainstem, and circumventricular organs, more readily than regions protected by the blood-brain barrier.

It has been revealed that the report authors noted that some studies have shown that GLP-1 receptor agonists may reduce the risk of cognitive impairment and dementia in people with type 2 diabetes. This may be due to cognitive concerns being linked to factors such as blood sugar, blood pressure, vascular health, and sleep.

Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline, “These findings are interesting, but like many of the other benefits associated with GLP-1 medications, a direct causal relationship has not yet been proven.”.

“Rather, the benefits appear to be more closely tied to the reduction in obesity and better control of diabetes,” he remarked.

Aurora noted that growing evidence supports the heart-brain connection.

She cited newly introduced findings from the Alzheimer’s Association’s landmark U.S. POINTER study presented at the Clinical Trials in Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) conference November 16–19 in Boston, MA.

The research highlighted that the structured lifestyle intervention program also improved heart health risk factors, such as:.

Sources indicate that “U.S. POINTER can change those risk factors within 24 months, and better heart health risk-factor control was linked with better cognition,” Aurora said. “We’re also interested to see whether adding a drug like a GLP-1 to a U.S. POINTER-style lifestyle program improves cognition in at-risk older adults more than the program alone.”.

To find out, the Alzheimer’s Association is funding the Prevention of Risk for Cognitive Decline through Combined Therapy (PROTECT-Cog) global phase 3 clinical trial.

PROTECT-Cog is a first-of-its-kind trial designed to evaluate whether combining a proven multidomain lifestyle intervention with a metabolism-targeting drug, like a GLP-1, can further reduce the risk of cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment, and dementia in at-risk older adults.

Dung Trinh, MD, internist at MemorialCare Medical Group and Chief Medical Officer of Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, CA, who also wasn’t involved in the review, told Healthline, “I often remind my patients that what’s good for the heart is generally good for the brain.”.

“The brain depends on a healthy cardiovascular system to deliver a constant supply of oxygen, glucose, and other nutrients. Conditions such as high blood pressure, diabetes, obesity, and high cholesterol can damage blood vessels, promote chronic inflammation, and increase the risk of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment,” he stated.

“Over time, these changes can also contribute to the development or progression of dementia.”.

Trinh added that while GLP-1 medications can improve several cardiometabolic risk factors, these improvements do not automatically translate into proven dementia prevention.

“Regular physical activity, a heart-healthy diet, adequate sleep, and management of cardiovascular risk factors remain essential strategies for maintaining brain health as we age,” he said.

When the report authors turned their attention to more stringent tests on semaglutide in people already living with early Alzheimer’s disease, the picture began to change.

Novo Nordisk’s EVOKE and EVOKE + Phase 3 Trials examined the efficacy of semaglutide in people with early stage Alzheimer’s disease.

The studies showed that while semaglutide produced changes in several disease-related biomarkers, it didn’t slow the progression of Alzheimer’s disease.

It has been revealed that this emphasizes that fixing metabolic complications might prevent cognitive decline in someone with obesity or diabetes. But it might not be enough to reverse the damage in someone with established Alzheimer’s disease, where profound synaptic loss and protein pathology have already occurred.

The review authors suggest that future research on obesity and diabetes should also include rigorous and specific cognitive testing.

Winter Weather Hits EV Range Hard. One Automaker Handles It Better Than Tesla

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (792 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, with the first signs of winter making their presence felt in some regions, it’s handy to remember that electric cars lose range when temperatures drop considerably.
  • This year, Tesla has been dethroned in the automaker rankings by an unexpected competitor, though the American EV manufacturer still holds the first two spots when it comes to individual models.
  • Recent findings suggest that polestar, the Swedish-headquartered, Chinese-owned organization that’s no longer allowed to sell cars in the United States after its inventory dries up, surpassed Tesla in the EV winter range rankings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, with the first signs of winter making their presence felt in some regions, it’s handy to remember that electric cars lose range when temperatures drop considerably. It happens across the board, but some automakers and models handle the cold better than others, and a upcoming study of over 59,000 EVs from Recurrent highlights which battery-powered cars retain the most range when the thermometer reaches 32°F (0°C).

This year, Tesla has been dethroned in the automaker rankings by an unexpected competitor, though the American EV manufacturer still holds the first two spots when it comes to individual models.

Recent findings suggest that polestar, the Swedish-headquartered, Chinese-owned organization that’s no longer allowed to sell cars in the United States after its inventory dries up, surpassed Tesla in the EV winter range rankings. The company’s models retain, on average, 88% of their range at 32°F (0°C) compared to ideal conditions, and 83% when the thermometer reads 20°F (-7°C).

Polestar 2 Arctic Circle Collection.

Meanwhile, Tesla, which has historically been the top performer in Recurrent’s rankings because of its early investments in heat pump systems and other winter optimizations, is second on the list this year, with an 85% average range retention at 32°F (0°C) and 77% at 20°F (-7°C).

Audi completes the automaker podium, with the German marque’s EVs retaining 79% of their range at 32°F (0°C) and 71% at 20°F (-7°C), according to Recurrent.

At this point, it’s worth noting that the comparison point for these figures is not the official EPA range figure, but the longest range achieved by a particular EV in ideal conditions, as recorded by Recurrent’s system. As a reminder, the firm gathers real-world data from EVs through owners who are willing to connect their cars to Recurrent’s servers.

Sources indicate that this year, Toyota is at the bottom of the list, with its EVs retaining just 70% of their summer range at freezing temperatures, with Mercedes-Benz not far ahead. Rivian ranked sixth, with an average range retention of 78% at 32°F (0°C), ahead of Hyundai and Porsche, but below Jaguar and Nissan.

When looking at individual electric models, Tesla still has the lead, with the heat pump-equipped Model S ranking first. The discontinued electric sedan retains 90% of its summer range at 32°F (0°C), followed by the soon-to-be-discontinued Cybertruck, with an average retention rate of 89%.

Despite Tesla losing to Polestar in the overall rankings, the Model S still has the lead in the models list.

Next up is the Polestar 2, the entry-level sedan that put Polestar on the map. The four-door EV can still deliver 88% of its summer range at 32°F (0°C), followed by the Tesla Model X with 87% and the Tesla Model 3 with 85%.

The popular Hyundai Ioniq 5 is 10th on the list, with an average range retention rate of 81%, below the Ioniq 6, Audi e-tron GT, Tesla Model Y, and Chevrolet Silverado EV, but above the Audi e-tron, Rivian R1S, and Nissan Ariya.

The pre-facelift Toyota bZ4X is at the bottom of the list with 70% of range available when the temperature is 32°F (0°C), ahead of the Mercedes-Benz EQS, Chevrolet Blazer EV, Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV, and Cadillac Lyriq. Interestingly, the Volkswagen e-Golf, which is over two decades old and doesn’t have a battery thermal management system, ranked above Cadillac’s Lyriq.

Industry observers note that on average, the 43 electric models included in Recurrent’s dataset retain 78% of their range in freezing temperatures compared to ideal conditions. That mentioned, the best EVs out there top out at 90% range retention, while the bottom of the pack gets only 70%.

A heat pump makes a world of difference when it comes to boosting winter range. Compared to traditional resistive heating systems, an EV equipped with a heat pump will have 8% more range in the winter, which can make the difference between getting home and calling a tow truck.

Sources indicate that speaking of home, home charging and preconditioning the car’s interior before setting off will also preserve precious miles when it’s time to go somewhere with a thick coat on. By using electricity from the grid to heat up the cabin, the battery will last longer before needing a recharge.

Tesla quietly sets up a firm at German machine maker EMAG’s HQ

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1008 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has registered a newly introduced German company whose business address is the headquarters of EMAG, a struggling machine-tool maker that builds production equipment for the gears inside humanoid robots.
  • But the paper trail is hard to ignore, and it lines up neatly with Tesla’s push to mass-produce Optimus.
  • The manufacturer is called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has registered a newly introduced German company whose business address is the headquarters of EMAG, a struggling machine-tool maker that builds production equipment for the gears inside humanoid robots.

Neither company confirmed a deal. But the paper trail is hard to ignore, and it lines up neatly with Tesla’s push to mass-produce Optimus.

The manufacturer is called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE. Germany’s official company register lists it under HRB 315756 at the Munich district court, with €120,000 in share capital and a business address of Austraße 24 in Salach, a small town east of Stuttgart. That’s EMAG’s home base.

It didn’t start out as a Tesla manufacturer. The register shows it was first entered on August 26 as “Blitz 26-299 SE,” a shell company. Law firms sell these pre-registered shells so buyers can skip weeks of incorporation paperwork, and Tesla renamed this one earlier this month.

Business Insider Germany, which reported the change based on a notice in the federal gazette, says three people run it: Maximilian Stromberger, Tesla Germany’s 33-year-old head of sales, an American robotics engineer, and the head of HR at Tesla’s Grünheide factory.

According to recent reports, the HR chief is the interesting name. You don’t need one to hold a passive stake in a supplier, but you do if you’re about to take on employees.

Neither Tesla nor EMAG answered Business Insider’s repeated requests for comment.

According to recent reports, local press near Salach has been on this for over a week. On November 23, the Stuttgarter Nachrichten reported that signs of a Tesla entry were piling up and that EMAG had briefed its workforce at a large staff meeting the week before. Business Insider dates that meeting to November 16.

Today, the same paper went further. It reports that around 220 EMAG employees will move to Tesla, that the two companies have been working together for some time, and that the deal is about humanoid robots. The full story is paywalled, and none of it has been confirmed by either manufacturer.

Sources indicate that EMAG, with roots going back to 1867, makes turning, grinding, and gear-cutting machines, mostly for car parts like transmissions and drivetrains. The auto slowdown hit it hard. A year ago, EMAG stated it would cut 455 jobs in Germany, roughly 300 of them in Salach, which is about a third of its domestic staff. It lost €42 million on €496 million of revenue in 2024, per Business Insider. It has been talking to potential investors ever since.

But EMAG has also been chasing a latest market. Its website has an entire section on manufacturing humanoid robot actuator parts: flexsplines, wave generators, and planetary gears.

The first two make up a strain wave gear, the compact, high-reduction gearbox used in robot joints. Planetary gears go in the bigger joints that carry more load. EMAG says its machines hold these parts to ISO 1328 Class 4 gear quality, with runout under 5 micrometers, and can repeat that in high-volume production.

It has been revealed that that’s right where Tesla says it’s stuck. On the Q3 earnings call last month, Musk called the hand Optimus’ main hardware problem and flagged custom gears as a reliability worry, as we reported at the time. Tesla is installing a Fremont line designed for a million robots a year, and the Optimus design it highlighted in 2022 used 28 structural actuators per robot. At that volume, you’re talking about tens of millions of actuators a year, many of them built around precision gears that few suppliers can make consistently.

It has been revealed that tesla moving directly into precision tooling highlights a brutal reality for robotics founders: software gets the spotlight, but high-tolerance actuator supply chains dictate your unit economics and scale. Building physical AI means mastering industrial manufacturing long before mass production begins. When navigating high-stakes hardware trade-offs and specialized talent, having early backers who have built hardware companies matters. Grove Ventures works hands-on from pre-seed with deeptech and AI founders, offering real operator experience to help scale complex physical architectures.

Sources indicate that tesla is already building the German side of this. In July, Tesla started recruiting in Reutlingen to develop and manufacture Optimus parts, including sensors, gearboxes, and actuators, plus the equipment to mass-produce them. Reutlingen is the former Manz site that Tesla took over in early 2025, along with about 300 of its employees.

Industry observers note that tesla has done this before. It agreed to buy Grohmann Engineering in Prüm in late 2016, which became Tesla Automation, and that unit absorbed the Manz operations. Tesla is also putting €3 billion into a Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin.

Sources indicate that tesla briefly acquired Wiferion in Germany. Tesla did buy the wireless charging startup in 2023, but it sold the business a few months later and kept the engineers.

Sources indicate that robots are still years away from your home, but solar isn’t. Battlefield 6 Season 2 delayed like many of us expected, but we're getting a new update and a bonus battle pass path

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026.
  • Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off.
  • In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

It has been revealed that given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something fresh in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj.

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension upgrade is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

According to recent reports, similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several upcoming customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

Driven: 2028 Porsche 718 Boxster EV Prototype Wags Its Tail Like a Mid-Engine Sports Car

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that there’s still a lot that Porsche won’t divulge about its forthcoming 2028 718 Boxster EV, including horsepower, battery capacity, range, pricing, or even its final, un-camouflaged looks.
  • In a recent development, whether you’re welcoming the Boxster’s EV transition or bemoaning the loss of its internal-combustion engines, particularly the iconic flat-six, we think anyone who drives the next-generation 983 Boxster will agree it’s fantastic.
  • In other words, this upcoming EV feels like a mid-engine Boxster, because that’s where the weight is concentrated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there’s still a lot that Porsche won’t divulge about its forthcoming 2028 718 Boxster EV, including horsepower, battery capacity, range, pricing, or even its final, un-camouflaged looks. But after some seat time around the handling course at the Porsche Experience Center Los Angeles, we now know what it feels like at—and a little bit beyond—its cornering limits.

In a recent development, whether you’re welcoming the Boxster’s EV transition or bemoaning the loss of its internal-combustion engines, particularly the iconic flat-six, we think anyone who drives the next-generation 983 Boxster will agree it’s fantastic. The steering, inherited from the 992.2 911 Carrera GTS, is eager and sharp, and rear-axle steering will also be available. You can feel the Boxster’s rear-biased weight distribution in the way its rear end steps out when lifting off the throttle.

In other words, this upcoming EV feels like a mid-engine Boxster, because that’s where the weight is concentrated. Other than some hypercars, such as the Rimac Nevera, the forthcoming electric Boxster rides atop one of the first EV platforms built around a two-seat sports car. The 800-volt battery pack lives entirely behind the passenger cabin, in the place the engine used to reside, which leads to a 40/60 front/rear weight distribution, similar to the gas-powered Boxster’s 45/55 split. And since there’s no battery under the floor, you sit as low as you would in any other sports car.

See all results for new 2028 Porsche 718 EV for sale near 20147.

In a recent development, we drove what will become the top Boxster model when it goes on sale after its formal debut in early 2027, but Porsche wouldn’t confirm what it will be called. S? GTS? These models wear Pirelli P Zero R Elect tires—and for the first time—mount on staggered-diameter wheels just like the latest 911. The tires measure 255/35ZR-20 up front and 305/30ZR-21 in back, which is more meat than even the last 718 Spyder RS. The tech giant isn’t saying how much power this Boxster’s single rear motor will make—all electric Boxsters will be rear-drive only—but they do claim the sprint to 60 mph will require less than 3.0 seconds. After experiencing being pinned to the seat by a few launch-control starts, the latest Boxster feels every bit that quick.

Porsche indicates this will be the quickest, most powerful Boxster with the highest cornering and braking performance, with a center of gravity that’s—no surprise—much lower than before. We can attest to feeling tons of grip, but can we feel the EV’s added weight? As the Boxster slithered through transitions and dove into apexes, we can’t say it felt heavy, although the squealing from its wide tires sounded at times more tortured than those we recall from the just-over-3000-pound gas-powered Boxster. Porsche says the Boxster EV’s curb weight will fall somewhere within that of the 911 lineup, which ranges from the 3350-pound Carrera to the 4000-pound Turbo S Cabriolet. Here’s hoping it’s toward the lower end of that range, which would be very light for an EV.

See all results for new 2028 Porsche 718 EV for sale near 20147.

According to recent reports, while this latest electric version looks like a Boxster and the low seating position feels like a Boxster, with a forward view of a swiftly disappearing hood, Porsche wanted to add some more nostalgic tie-ins by way of fabricated engine noises and simulated shifts. The Taycan got a similar E-Shift feature earlier this year, but while the Taycan’s engine noises weren’t modeled after a specific engine, the Boxster’s very much pays homage to its past. The Boxster’s E-Shift, which is controlled by a knob on the steering wheel and can shift automatically or be controlled by steering wheel paddles, mimics the 981 Boxster GTS’s 3.4-liter flat-six, which Porsche engineers say is the high-water mark for flat-six wails. They told us emissions compromises to the most recent flat-sixes made them choose that one from circa 2015. That said, there’s a bit of revisionist history going on with the electric Boxster’s 8000-rpm “redline” versus the actual 7600-rpm redline in its 981 muse. Either way, the noise emanating from the two speakers—one inside the cabin, one outside—absolutely sounds like a flat-six.

Industry observers note that although the synthesized sound is a solid re-creation, we do think it would be easy to identify the real from the facsimile in a blindfolded test. There’s a lot of nuance going on in the sounds of a flat-six belting to redline—intake and exhaust noise, valve and other mechanical clatter—and it’s hard to generate all of that from a couple speakers. That said, after doing a few hot laps with the system on, we believe it adds to the experience, and it felt weird to switch over to silent and shift-free lapping. We think we’d use this more in a sports car like the Boxster than in the four-door Taycan sedan.

What else did we learn? As before, the 983 Boxster has both front and rear trunks, and its NACS charge port, which is hidden behind a powered door in the middle of the rear bumper, is the first from Porsche to accommodate both AC and DC charging. Today’s Cayenne and Taycan electrics have separate ports for AC and DC with the NACS only handling DC charging.

Officially, there won’t be any gas-powered Boxster variants, but who knows what the lifecycle might hold, especially if early sales disappoint. After all, remember when the previous generation went four-cylinder only, but then the flat-six made a reappearance a few years later? While we’re as sad as anyone to see the flat-six and manual transmission leave the Boxster lineup, we think that anyone who drives the new one will agree it’s a great-handling sports car.

By 2040, 51% of People Living with HIV Could Be Over 50

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Advances in antiretroviral therapy (ART) have helped people living with HIV live longer, contributing to a growing population of older adults with the virus.
  • It has been revealed that in fact, a recent report published in The Lancet HIV projects that approximately 51% of people living with HIV worldwide will be over age 50 by 2040.
  • The report’s authors emphasized the “pressing need” for HIV prevention and screening services tailored to older adults, who face additional age-related challenges when accessing care.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Advances in antiretroviral therapy (ART) have helped people living with HIV live longer, contributing to a growing population of older adults with the virus.

It has been revealed that in fact, a recent report published in The Lancet HIV projects that approximately 51% of people living with HIV worldwide will be over age 50 by 2040. An estimated 96% of these older adults will live in low- and middle-income countries.

The report’s authors emphasized the “pressing need” for HIV prevention and screening services tailored to older adults, who face additional age-related challenges when accessing care.

These challenges include stigma related to both age and HIV, a higher burden of chronic health conditions, taking multiple medications, delayed diagnoses, physical limitations, and increased financial and social vulnerability.

Factors like these “influence HIV risk for older adults in complex and dynamic ways,” according to the report authors.

Several factors have contributed to the growing population of older adults living with HIV, including:.

Sources indicate that many adults over age 50 who are living with HIV acquired the virus during young adulthood in the late 1990s and early 2000s. During that period, some experienced prolonged periods of uncontrolled HIV and exposure to older ART medications with more severe side effects, which may have contributed to long-term inflammation and other health complications.

William Schaffner, MD, professor in the Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline, “That older persons with HIV are on track to outnumber younger persons with HIV infection is a double-barreled success story.”.

In a recent development, “First, the effective treatment of persons with HIV infection has resulted in the expectation of normal or near-normal lifespans; thus, more older persons living with HIV infection,” he said. “This is a great success; both in creating effective, easy-to-use medicines as well as developing medical care systems that can reach such patients and provide lifetime care.”.

Schaffner said the second success has been educating younger people about HIV prevention, helping reduce upcoming infections.

In a recent development, older adults also account for a growing proportion of fresh HIV diagnoses. They are more likely to receive a diagnosis later in the course of infection, which can delay treatment and increase the risk of serious health complications and death.

Mathematical models project that the average age of people living with HIV worldwide will increase from 41 in 2025 to 50 by 2040, largely driven by demographic shifts in low- and middle-income countries.

While the World Health Organization (WHO) does not specify an upper age limit for HIV testing in its published overview, U.S. guidelines focus on specific age groups.

According to recent reports, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends routine HIV testing for people ages 13 to 64, and the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommends testing for people ages 15 to 65.

In a recent development, however, these age limits don’t mean older adults shouldn’t be tested for HIV, as both U.S. organizations also recommend testing older adults who may be at risk.

Older adults can still be sexually active and have a chance of acquiring HIV. Certain physical changes that come with age, such as thinning of vaginal tissue, may also increase the risk of HIV infection.

Despite these risks, older adults are often overlooked in HIV prevention campaigns, research, and clinical trials. The report’s authors say more needs to be done to address these gaps.

“Targeted and tailored HIV prevention and screening services for older adults are a pressing global need,” the report authors stated.

Schaffner agreed with this and added, “Increasing the effectiveness of diagnosis and treatment of HIV infection in older adults will increase their expectation of a healthier, longer life.”.

The report recommends several approaches to improving HIV prevention and screening among older adults, including:.

While Schaffner noted that HIV treatment has “advanced spectacularly over the past 20 years,” making it possible for people living with HIV to lead longer, healthier lives, access to these treatments remains a challenge in many parts of the world.

Inside the Hot Wheels Design Center

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1501 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The most incredible toy store on Earth—Mattel’s Handler Team Center, the company’s design hub tucked away on a nondescript stretch of road in El Segundo, California—is all these things and more.
  • It has been revealed that from a giant mural, Mattel’s cofounders, Elliot and Ruth Handler, smile down on the building’s front lobby, where life-size Hot Wheels vehicles appear poised for action, and wall art displays iconic Mattel playsets and characters from the firm’s inception through the present day.
  • There’s speed (the cars reach what would equate to 297 mph at full scale), experimentation (do you go with a weightier or sleeker car?), and crashes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

State-of-the-art car garage. Museum. Mad scientist’s lab. Stuntworks. The most incredible toy store on Earth—Mattel’s Handler Team Center, the company’s design hub tucked away on a nondescript stretch of road in El Segundo, California—is all these things and more.

It has been revealed that from a giant mural, Mattel’s cofounders, Elliot and Ruth Handler, smile down on the building’s front lobby, where life-size Hot Wheels vehicles appear poised for action, and wall art displays iconic Mattel playsets and characters from the firm’s inception through the present day. Down at the very far end of the lobby, the Epic Loop screams for attention. It is an eleven-foot-tall Hot Wheels duo racetrack with side-by-side loops. Visitors are encouraged to re-create a game played by millions of young Hot Wheels fans by climbing a flight of stairs and sending a die-cast car of their choice down the competing tracks in a race to launch their car into a bucket that marks the finish line.

There’s speed (the cars reach what would equate to 297 mph at full scale), experimentation (do you go with a weightier or sleeker car?), and crashes. Lots of crashes.

The message is clear: This place is a temple of wild design and outrageous fun.

Push deeper into the 200,000-square-foot building (which once housed an aerospace company), and you arrive at the beating heart of the world’s most famous brand on four wheels: the Hot Wheels Design Center.

Every inch of this place is filled with reminders of Hot Wheels’ storied past, as well as the schematics and prototypes that map out its high-tech future.

Oh, and there are toy cars. Everywhere. Toy cars on tables, toy cars in pristine display cases fit for the Louvre, smashed-up toy cars piled in cluttered cubicles. It’s every kid’s and every collector’s dream come true—as well as a dream come true for the people working inside these walls.

The Hot Wheels die-cast design team sits together in a ring, their cubicles surrounding long tables that serve as a communal space for collaboration, display, tinkering, and sharing the occasional Friday morning donut.

Recent findings suggest that black light-blocking hoods arch over each cubicle, giving them the feeling of a custom car garage or the messiest kid’s bedroom ever. Within the cubicles, toy cars in every stage of design are piled up against keyboards, and the interior cube walls are plastered with pinned-up artwork, schematics, and toy racks.

Sources indicate that underneath one of these hoods sits Dwayne Vance, a longtime Hot Wheels designer who is now manager of product design and steers the visual direction of every graphic in die-cast for Hot Wheels. Vance has worked for other huge brands like DC Comics, EA Games, and Texaco, and his passion for art and automotive extends well beyond the walls of this place, from his creation and curation of art reveals to his own book series, Masters of Chicken Scratch, devoted to futuristic and fantasy hot-rod artwork and designs.

An oversize rendering he created in the early 2000s of the Hot Wheels classic car Bone Shaker, with the word Attitude boldly emblazoned across the top, hangs over his work area. Unlike many of his fellow designers, Vance’s cubicle is neatly arranged and organized. “It helps me creatively to sit down in a nice clean space,” he notes. Some of his favorite cars fill his shelves, as does his Matty Award.

Industry observers note that every designer has particular strengths, so when Hot Wheels decided it was time to breathe fresh life into the Custom Camaro, Vance was part of a small group of designers tasked with cooking up new concepts. “We wanted a licensed vehicle but with an extreme custom,” indicates Staff Product Designer Fraser Campbell. “Knowing Dwayne’s work, I knew he’d create something wild.”.

In a recent development, as pens hit paper in a flurry of ideas, the designers soon faced a challenge not uncommon for Hot Wheels: the ticking clock. Campbell explains that when putting together a year’s lineup for initial concept review (ICR), where the cars get evaluated and refined to ensure a good overall mix before things move along to production, the designers need to fill in any perceived gaps—promptly.

“Several of us designers were going to be working on the Camaro, but the other guys got so busy that it was up to me to finish the project,” claims Vance. “So, I was like, ‘Okay, cool!’ I got to spend maybe two weeks on the design—it wasn’t a lot. One thing we don’t have here is the luxury of time.”.

But just like race car drivers behind the wheels of the cars they’re inspired by, Hot Wheels designers thrive under pressure.

Vance began where he always begins—sketching. “I usually just go straight to Photoshop. I have a monitor on my desk, and I actually sketch right on the monitor,” he explains. But the motor muse can strike at any time and any place, and in the case of this redesign, it hit Vance at thirty thousand feet.

Recent findings suggest that “I was on a plane and pulled out my sketchbook and put down some initial ideas,” he says. He typically has a sketchbook within reach, but any piece of paper will do. “Sometimes I’ll draw a little piece of a car on a sticky note,” he says.

In a recent development, whenever the muse speaks, he listens—and gives it a soundtrack with the help of a little music and his headphones. “I listen to a lot of deep house when I’m drawing in my cube,” he indicates. “It’s got good energy and is easy to draw to.”.

For the 2023 Custom ’68 Camaro reboot, Vance aimed to commemorate the past while bringing it into the future, inspired by what he saw happening in modern muscle-car culture. Instead of trying to restore vintage rides to their original settings, he saw customizers on a mission to “make muscle cars beautiful again” with new engines, new suspensions, and new brake systems—“they were just chopping them up.”.

Vance studied the work of boundary-pushing, high-end car builders like Hoonigan, and when he saw a ’69 Mustang that a customizer had retrofitted with an LS1 Corvette engine, a vision began to crystallize.

“I thought, how fun would it be to do that to the Camaro?”.

In a recent development, he broke out the chop saw in his mind and went to town, cutting out body panels to reveal the exhaust system sticking out of the side of the car. He lopped off the whole front bumper, exposing much of the car’s underpinnings. He added a recessed grille with an air intake, and in keeping with the Hot Wheelizing philosophy of pushing the limits while keeping it recognizable, he stayed true to the Camaro’s signature headlight shape.

In a recent development, vance also created a hood bulge that hints at the powerful engine underneath and bolted on vertical fins in the back, inspired by the Le Mans Prototype (LMP) race cars used in endurance racing. “The fins help these race cars with cornering, giving them friction so they can stay grounded and accelerate. I thought, let’s add that to a muscle car!”.

He then hacked off the rear bumpers to expose the roll cage, which he claims, “really did something ultra-aggressive to the car.”.

When it came time to create the 2026 Custom ’68 Camaro for this book, Vance again engaged in some role-playing—but this time he stepped into the shoes of someone with a very different perspective from a cyberpunk racer.

“I put myself in the Hot Wheels collector’s position—I wanted something that really celebrates the brand and yells, ‘Hot Wheels!’”.

To that end, Vance gave his punked-up ’23 model a sleek new paint and decoration job. The base color is a rich Spectraflame red; the side panels are emblazoned with massive Hot Wheels flames; the hood declares Hot Wheels loud and proud; and the side panels and roof feature the number 68, a nod to the year Elliot Handler started Hot Wheels. Vance also added classic race wheels typically found on 1960s stock cars to complete what he calls a modernized classic.

“I want a collector to see this and say, ‘Man, I want this book, but I really, really want the car!’”.

Tech Report: VW Will Pay German Drivers To Plug In Their EVs. Even If The Grid Never Uses Their Power

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that plug your electric Volkswagen in at 8 in the evening, unplug it at 6 the next morning, and you could earn €2.40 while you sleep.
  • We already wrote about Germany’s strategy to allow parked EVs to earn money.
  • Industry observers note that elli will pay €0.24 for each hour the EV is plugged in, provided each session lasts at least three hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that plug your electric Volkswagen in at 8 in the evening, unplug it at 6 the next morning, and you could earn €2.40 while you sleep. How much electricity would your car have to send back to the grid for that money? Potentially none. Starting in December, VW’s charging subsidiary Elli will pay eligible German drivers for the hours their car spends plugged in at home, even if it doesn’t actually supply any power during that time.

We already wrote about Germany’s strategy to allow parked EVs to earn money. Upcoming rules made it easier to account for electricity stored in a car and later sold back to the grid, even for homes that can generate their own power through solar panels. That left a fairly notable question for anyone with an EV in the driveway: How much could you actually earn? Now, Volkswagen has put a number on it.

Industry observers note that elli will pay €0.24 for each hour the EV is plugged in, provided each session lasts at least three hours. The bonus tops out at €60 a month, or €720 yearly. Earning the full amount takes 250 hours a month, a little over eight hours a night. In the app, you tell Elli when you need the car and how much charge you want when you leave.

Elli will handle charging and discharging around your schedule, but to make this work you need its 11-kilowatt bidirectional charger with vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capability. That costs €1,995 without installation, and your home also needs a compatible smart electricity meter for everything to work. Owners can register now, then check eligibility at launch and get an installation quote before ordering.

The thing is, even if you collect every euro of the first-year bonus, that still leaves €1,275 of the charger’s price to cover, plus whatever the electrician charges to install it.

Industry observers note that not all VW EVs have bidirectional charging. It introduced this feature on its European models in 2023, but it states there are around one million eligible EVs in Europe, about a third of which are in Germany. The offer covers Volkswagen, Cupra and Škoda, and the charger supports 400- and 800-volt vehicles, even if the latter is not present in any of the three brands’ vehicles.

Elli says it aims to expand into more European markets in 2027 and offer a separate vehicle-to-home system so owners can save rooftop solar power for use after dark. A one-year trial involving 20 German households logged roughly 85,000 combined charger hours online and more than 6,500 charging and discharging sessions, the company stated.

Sources indicate that VW calculates that €720 could buy enough electricity to drive an ID.3 Neo nearly 10,000 miles (16,000 km), assuming €0.33 per kWh and the car’s official WLTP consumption. So it may not offset the full cost of the bidirectional charger, but that’s still a lot of free driving for just keeping the car plugged in overnight.
